title: [Radix Cache] Sync Rust TreeCore and make it the default
body:
Use Rust as the default unified tree core and resolve unsupported configurations to Python in one central place. Synchronize these Python behaviors:

| Original Python PR | Rust change |
| --- | --- |
| [#38356 — Logical-page placement](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38356) | Preserve `rotation_base` through insertion and splitting, and reject incompatible grafts before transferring KV ownership. |
| [#37503 — HiCache accounting](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37503) | Count every unbacked Full-KV eviction within a native step, including cascades, and report `tracked_unbacked_tokens`. |
| [#37795 — Eviction-policy configuration](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37795) | Forward SLRU's `protected_threshold` and validate policy parameters. The cutoff orders probationary nodes before protected nodes while preserving LRU order within each segment; the original policy came from [#18843](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18843). |
| [#34012 — T-LRU eviction](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34012) | Port tail-first eviction with integer or floating-point `threshold` and `next_prompt_estimate`, preserving Python’s arithmetic order and exact integer/float comparisons. Track path depth and branch high-water history through device/host insertion and splits, retaining history after eviction so repeated trimming stops at the original budget. |
| [#33777 — Write-back host pressure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33777) | Preserve insertion order when reclaiming Full host duplicates, including removals and new backups. Register new copies at acknowledgment so pending internal splits publish their prefix before their suffix. Retain device-resident SWA host backups under SWA pressure, matching Python's Full-only duplicate prepass; ordinary host-only SWA eviction remains available. |
| [#38462 — Host-duplicate reclamation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38462) | Honor `SGLANG_HICACHE_SKIP_HOST_DUPLICATE_RECLAIM` in native eviction. |
| [#38269 — SWA layout-aware reuse](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38269) | Use the allocator's actual request-ring capability for SWA matching. This preserves ring prefix reuse without HiCache and rejects paged-SWA hits without the required window, including DSV4.1 encoder replay + DSpark + HiCache configurations from [#38798](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38798). |
| [#39283 — SWA buffer-mode prefetch](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39283) | Port `swa_tombstone_ranges` and `attach_swa_window`, including repairs that split existing nodes, preserving KV ownership, locks, pending write-through actions and namespace/page offsets. |
| [#37507 — Unified-memory HiCache](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37507) | Preserve exact Full-row anchors for SWA load-back, including resident-row holes, and resolve current physical SWA rows before backup after compaction. |
| [#40680 — Internal Mamba write-back](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40680) | Back up internal Mamba state before eviction, wait for acknowledgment and retain resident Full KV. Reclaim host-state capacity first; preserve the legacy drop on allocation failure and device state on submission/acknowledgment exceptions. |
| [#40712 — Internal SWA write-back](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40712) | Preserve eligible internal SWA windows before eviction. Pause for the controller to reclaim capacity for the whole unbacked window and finish its host backup, then resume safely after success or allocation failure. |

Centralized Python fallback applies to both default and explicit Rust selection for:

- Session-aware caching.
- C128 or other unsupported components.
- Custom component overrides.
- Non-Linux platforms.
- PyTorch versions outside 2.11–2.13, or unrecognized versions.
- Devices other than CPU or CUDA.
- Installations containing neither the Rust extension nor its sources.
- Source builds with a missing or unusable Rust toolchain.

Trusted bundled extensions need no compiler. Supported configurations continue to surface build, import and runtime errors. Unexpected native panics now become `RuntimeError`, with the original panic retained as the cause, so Python crash handlers can report the failure and coordinate shutdown. The native mutex still refuses poisoned state; this does not recover or reuse a failed core. Production, inspection and bigram bindings are covered.

T-LRU supports integer and floating-point parameters with Python's operation order, rounding and exact integer/float comparisons, including NaN and infinity. Integer-only parameters retain the exact tail-budget path. Mixed integer estimates must fit i128; larger values raise `OverflowError` at construction, and checked native addition panics on overflow. Priority evaluation uses native scalar arithmetic without allocation or Python callbacks. T-LRU adds two counters per node (16 bytes on 64-bit platforms); its ancestor history walk runs only for T-LRU and costs O(path nodes).

One insertion-ordered `NodeSet` serves device leaves, host leaves and Full host duplicates. It preserves constant-time membership/removal, amortized constant-time insertion and exact-size iteration. Leaf eviction still ranks candidates in its policy heap; Full duplicate reclamation follows Python's insertion order.

Auxiliary eviction respects each component's own transfer/request locks. An unrelated Full load or expanded SWA backup must not pin independently restored auxiliary state. Actual transfer sources/destinations and Full leaf guards remain protected. Deferred Mamba and SWA eviction revalidate the victim after the controller's backup attempt, preserve device state on submission/acknowledgment exceptions, and retain progress when host allocation fails. The controller uses the existing transfer and ACK path; the optional finish hooks support native pause/resume without requiring inline backends to implement them.

Hybrid transfer plans cross the binding in Python's component order, removing native HashMap nondeterminism. The shared host allocator now follows main's pool-name ordering from #40512; paired host-pressure expectations follow that order. Main's unified-memory decode host pools (#39478) use the shared controller path and need no separate native port.

The real default-cache test exercises construction, insertion and matching without factory mocks. Shared inspections replace native-specific test skips. This update removes the internal-SWA Rust skip and five obsolete Full+SWA+Mamba HiCache skips, enabling the now-supported hybrid fixtures. Legitimate configuration-applicability guards remain. Session cases in a Rust-selected run exercise centralized Python fallback. External backends must implement the two abstract SWA repair methods; the README documents this and the optional deferred-eviction hooks.

Validation of current head `82181482bb`, based on main `182f62d2de`:

- The latest commit corrects one shared hybrid Mamba test expectation: after SWA splits a 128-token prefix, only 64 tokens have Full host copies, while all 128 Full tokens remain cached and become usable after Mamba load-back. Both backends reproduce that layout and return the identical 128 device indices. The test now checks `full_kv_hit_length` before load-back and retains the exact returned-prefix, node and revived-state assertions afterward. No runtime code or applicability guard changed.
- The actual shared write-back methods passed **32/32 cases across Python and Rust** (all six Mamba and ten SWA configurations); paired write-through controls also passed. These use real CPU allocators, eviction, load-back commit, ACK cleanup and sanity checks; only device placement and host DMA/allocation boundaries were simulated. [Base](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36062047566) stage C and the final [Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36062046996) B300 shard remain pending or running on the corrected head.
- **Current-head CI: all 11 CPU shards / 714 executed files passed**, with unchanged per-file skip counts. Native **915 passed**, one existing ignored; integration **391 passed**, one existing CUDA skip; panic **14 passed**; registry **30 passed**; real-default smoke **6 passed**; DP prefill **13 passed**. The panic file ran through the actual CI entry point. Every completed test log checks out merge `d55509ad89b`, which includes only documentation changes from newer main `a1eb691ab5`. Lint and all nine Extra simulator tests passed.
- **Current-head shared GPU suites passed on both backends:** each ran 2,769 tests with **1,292 passes / 1,477 configuration skips**, zero failures and zero built-in retries. Individual outcomes match: all ten newly enabled hybrid cases and all ten SWA write-back configurations passed, including the repaired page-64 hybrid Mamba case. Both jobs tested merge `d55509ad89b`; the Rust shard passed all eleven files and the Python shard all fifteen.
- **Current-head NVIDIA stage A passed all five files: 63 passing cases and two existing FA3 hardware skips** on RTX 5090. All three serving launches selected `RustUnifiedTreeCore`; no retry was needed. All **17 non-B300 Extra GPU shards passed**, including all H100/H200/B200 groups, 18 hybrid bit-exact tests (nine Rust and nine Python), paired DSV4 KL/HiCache coverage and real unified-memory HiCache round trips. Extra B300 is queued for shared runner capacity. **All 20/20 Base stage-B GPU shards passed**. **Stage C has passed 12/15 GPU shards**, with every completed log audited: all B200/H200/GB300/H100 groups and the first H20 shard. Native PP2/TP2 Mooncake HiCache executed successful prefetches and kept GSM8K at 0.700 across a cache flush; native Mamba branching/KL and DSV4 cached-prefix recall also passed. Two H20 shards and B300 are queued, with no current failed job. This is not an all-CI-green claim.
- A transient tracing-test startup port collision (`TCPStore` / `EADDRINUSE`) cleared on Base attempt 2 with no source change. The retried shard passed all six files; the actual tracing method ran and passed, both servers selected Rust, and there was no repeated port error or test-level retry. All formerly blocked Base stage-B jobs now pass and the gate has advanced to stage C; completed successes, including both shared suites, are retained. No production workaround or threshold change was added.
- Main's [#41162](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41162) repairs the stale DP speculative-prefill test mock from #40858. That fix is in the base, with no unrelated test change in this PR's diff. The rebase passed **105 tests and 115 subtests** covering DP coordination, registry/default routing, native panic handling and updated pool budgets.
- The original port checks passed feature-enabled Clippy with warnings denied, Python/native formatting, import sorting, selected lint and spelling. Paired tests cover whole-window/page-rounded SWA capacity, successful and failed backups, submission/ACK exceptions, component locks, buffer-only mode, runtime policy updates and hybrid Mamba cascades. Both backend suites collect the enabled GPU cases. Local Torch is CPU-only; simulated transfers do not establish GPU numerical equivalence.

GPU evidence below is **historical coverage of preceding head `211c4be57e`**, not validation of the new SWA/panic changes:

| NVIDIA coverage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Rust shared suite | 1,266 passed with 1,465 existing applicability skips; entire shard 15/15 files passed. |
| Full cache accuracy/branching | Eight tests passed across real Python/Rust cores; GSM8K 0.965 on both, mean KL below 0.00059 against the 0.0025 limit. |
| DSV4 Full+SWA | 14 Rust and 14 Python methods passed, including DSpark/EAGLE/plain L3 restore. |
| Mamba and GLM-5.2 HiCache | All 10 Mamba tests and both GLM L3 tests passed, including full-prefix prefetch after flushing. |
| File HiCache / speculative Mooncake | File restore reused 768 tokens; Mooncake preserved acceptance 8.000 and reused 960 storage-cached tokens. |
| Linker / checkpoint / canary | GLM branching/multiturn, int8 Mamba checkpoint and mock-EAGLE canary tests passed. |
| Base 2-GPU shards 4 and 5 | Both passed after retrying runner-communication failures on the unchanged head and merge commit; no test-level retry was needed. |

All 18 [Extra NVIDIA GPU shards](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35953815270) passed on that preceding head. [Base](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35953815511) had no remaining NVIDIA failure, with three large-GPU jobs still queued before this push. Fresh CI must validate the new head. Unclassified AMD runtime signals and unrelated NPU/XPU/Xeon failures remain outside this NVIDIA-focused follow-up; this does not claim all-platform CI success.

Rotation has simulated-rank/core coverage; production allocator selection and serving E2E remain outside that coverage. CPU transfer regressions mock physical DMA and do not establish GPU numerical equivalence. No accuracy threshold or runtime skip was added to address failures.

title: [ROCm] GLM-5.2 decode path: decode-shaped MoE/MLA tiles, split speculative softmax, and bf16 GEMM routing
body:
## Motivation

Four changes on the GLM-5.2 decode path on gfx950, found by profiling a
GLM-5.2-MXFP4 TP8/EP1 server at 104k context. They are all the same shape: at
decode batch sizes these kernels leave a 256-CU part mostly idle, and none of
them is made faster by doing less arithmetic.

- two of them launch a handful of workgroups because the tile or the reduction
  was sized for a regime decode never enters;
- one spends more time in launch overhead than in work;
- one lands on torch because a tuned table keyed on `(N, K)` has no entry for
  the shape and does not fall back to a neighbour.

Together they are **+5.7%** end to end on that configuration.

## Modifications

**`moe`: fold the padded-row fill into the shared-expert append kernel.**
`_post_process_topk_ids` bracketed the aiter shared-expert append with two
separate fills over the padded region -- one for the routed ids, one for the
weights -- three launches for a shape whose total work is a couple of
microseconds, once per MoE layer per step. The append kernel already writes
every one of those elements, so it fills the padded region itself. The id fold
requires EPLB remap off, since it relies on `pad_fill_id = 0` commuting with
`remap(0) = 0`; the weight fold additionally excludes the per-rank shared-slot
kernel, which has no shared-slot weights to zero. Where either precondition
does not hold, the separate fills run exactly as before.

**`mla`: size the absorb BMM tiles for decode.** aiter's config table has no
entry for the MLA absorb shapes, so decode falls into a bucket tuned for square
GEMMs (`BLOCK_SIZE_M=64, BLOCK_SIZE_N=256`). The grid is
`(heads, cdiv(M, BM) * cdiv(N, BN))`, so at 16 heads per rank and `N <= 512`
that launches 16-32 workgroups on a 256-CU part: starved of workgroups, not of
bandwidth or flops. This sizes the tile so the grid covers the machine and then
stops -- it does not keep splitting, because the kernel quantizes its own A tile
per token group, so every extra workgroup repeats that work (at M=200/N=512 an
unbounded split is 3.7x slower than the starved table entry).

**`spec`: split the vocab-wide speculative softmax across CTAs.** Speculative
sampling reduces across the vocabulary at every draft step and at verify. torch
reduces each row with one block, so at the row counts speculation actually runs
(1 to 32) a 154880-wide row occupies a handful of blocks, and it is read three
times. `temperature_softmax()` splits each row across CTAs -- partial
max+sumexp, an online-softmax merge, then normalize -- and folds the temperature
divide into the first pass, which drops the separate pass that materialized
`logits / temperatures`. It hands the call back to torch above the row count
where one block per row already fills the GPU, so callers use it
unconditionally.

`fast_sample`'s argmax gets the same treatment by routing it to the existing
`row_argmax()`, which already lands this optimization for the dspark accept
path. No second implementation is added: a split argmax written for this path
is 4.7-42% faster below 32 rows but 3x *slower* above it, where it fell back to
torch, and those are the verify row counts at higher concurrency.

**`linear`: route the bf16 decode shapes aiter's tuned table misses.** The aiter
tuned GEMM keys its table on `(N, K)` and does not fall back to a neighbour, so
a shape the table never saw lands on torch. A decode step hits one of those 79
times -- the MLA q up-projection, `(2048, 2048)` -- where torch runs at 8.4 us
against a 1.05 us weight-bandwidth roofline while aiter's own Triton a16w16
kernel does it in 5.0 us. What is missing is the routing, not a kernel.

The gate is `K` rather than a list of shapes: a list keyed on `(N, K)` is what
makes the aiter table miss these shapes to begin with, and a different tensor
parallel split moves every `N`. It is also bounded in the row count, because
what torch is slow at is the weight-bandwidth-bound regime decode lives in and a
prefill chunk is its opposite -- a 32768-token chunk is 1.25-1.44x *slower* on
the Triton kernel, so prefill must not be routed. `lm_head`, `(19360, 6144)`, is
1.33x slower there and stays where it was.

## Accuracy Tests

Every change is either bit-identical by construction or checked against a
reference before any timing.

| change | property | how it is checked |
|---|---|---|
| moe padded fill | bit-identical | the append kernel already writes those elements; folded only where the preconditions above hold |
| mla absorb tiles | bit-identical | same kernel, different tile; compared at every admitted M |
| `temperature_softmax` | fp32-accurate | vs a float64 reference, not vs torch, which is not ground truth at this width |
| `row_argmax` routing | bit-identical | vs `torch.argmax`, including the sampled index and the `gather` that consumes it |
| linear routing | bit-identical at M=1 | max rel diff 1.7e-4 at M=6, with the error against a float64 reference *equal* to torch's -- not accuracy traded for speed |

`temperature_softmax` against float64, MI355X, vocab 154880:

```
rows      this PR       torch       row sum deviation
   1     3.42e-11    3.42e-11                7.44e-08
   2     2.67e-11    3.27e-11                6.07e-08
   6     2.42e-09    2.89e-09                3.62e-08
  12     3.47e-10    3.47e-10                8.26e-08
  32     3.34e-09    3.34e-09                1.44e-07
  48     1.30e-09    1.30e-09                9.04e-08
  84     2.89e-09    2.89e-09                1.29e-07
```

`row_argmax` matches `torch.argmax` exactly at all seven row counts, and returns
the lowest index on an all-tied row, which ROCm's argmax does not guarantee
(#26358).

A GLM-5.2-MXFP4 TP8 server on an fp8 KV cache comes up and serves correctly with
`--dsa-decode-backend triton`, checked against prompts with verifiable answers
on both arms of every end-to-end run below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Kernel level

`benchmark/kernels/bench_bf16_linear_routing.py` ships with this PR and needs no
server or model weights. It runs both arms in one process and interleaves them
ABBA, so the clock drift that moves kernels this small by ~10% lands on both;
the figure reported is the ratio's spread, not either arm's.

The speculative reductions, MI355X, vocab 154880, fp32, under CUDA graph replay
(the path decode runs on), us/call:

```
rows |  softmax: torch     PR    speedup  spread |  argmax: torch     PR    speedup  spread
   1 |           52.37   6.03      8.7x   23.36% |          12.00   4.61      2.6x    2.34%
   2 |           53.62   6.45      8.3x    0.79% |          34.48   4.71      7.3x    7.93%
   6 |           55.92   7.88      7.1x    0.45% |          34.65   5.24      6.6x    1.15%
  12 |           58.31   9.75      6.0x    1.51% |          34.04   5.75      5.9x    0.95%
  32 |           65.09  20.78      3.1x    0.75% |          33.98   8.70      3.9x    0.90%
  48 |           76.94  76.75      1.0x    0.29% |          36.97  11.19      3.3x    0.67%
  84 |           94.13  94.13      1.0x    0.22% |          45.80  12.28      3.7x    0.65%
```

Rows 48 and 84 in the softmax column are it handing the call back to torch above
its row limit: the harness measuring one implementation against itself, which is
the control for the rest of the column. The 23% spread at one row is the ratio's
own spread over six interleaved rounds on a 6 us kernel; every other point is
under 2%.

In eager the launch cost is not amortized and the softmax win shrinks to
1.1-1.4x; this is a graph-replay optimization and the docstrings say so.

The other two, from their own commits: the MoE append fold is 4.74 -> 1.61 us at
one row and flat in the row count, because what it removes is two launches
rather than work; the MLA `w_vc` absorb (N=256, K=512) goes from 18.1 to 3.6 us
at M=48, and `w_kc` from 12.9 to 3.1.

### End to end

Steady-state decode throughput per user, median over a 150 s window at
concurrency 1 and 2, geometric mean of the two. Base and patched arms were
interleaved across the session rather than run back to back, so linear drift
lands on both:

```
GLM-5.2-MXFP4 · TP8/EP1 · concurrency 1 and 2 · fp8 KV · 104k context
EAGLE 5/6 · --dsa-decode-backend triton · hierarchical cache off

                    vs base     read-to-read spread
base                      =     0.59%  (three reads)
three kernels        +3.94%     0.14%  (two reads)
+ linear routing     +5.67%     0.05%  (two reads)

geometric mean is over the two concurrencies; separately, at +linear routing
  concurrency 1     +4.95%
  concurrency 2     +6.39%
```

The effect is about ten times the baseline's own read-to-read spread. Within it,
the absorb tile accounts for +0.85% and the linear routing for +1.66%; the
softmax and the MoE fold make up the rest.

A trace replay of the same model (aiperf, 1800 s), one read per arm, covering
the three kernel changes only -- it was taken before the linear routing existed:

```
GLM-5.2-MXFP4 · TP8/EP1 · concurrency 1 · fp8 KV · 104k context
EAGLE 5/6 · --dsa-decode-backend triton · hierarchical cache off

per-user throughput, p90     +3.55%
per-GPU total throughput     +1.62%
```

Both arms completed the same number of profiled requests with no dropped
errors, so neither figure comes from a shortened or partly failed run.

Two harnesses with different workloads and different statistics -- a median over
a fixed-shape load and a p90 over a trace replay -- agree on the magnitude for
the part they both cover.

### What this does not claim

Neither figure is a position on a published curve. Both are paired A/B deltas on
one configuration, taken with hierarchical cache off, so they are not comparable
to a leaderboard point.

The end-to-end numbers were taken with the local split argmax described above
rather than with `row_argmax`; the difference between the two is ~1.5 us of a
12.6 ms decode step at these batch sizes, so the tables were not re-taken. The
trace-replay arms are one read each, so drift is not bracketed there; only the
first harness has repeat reads (0.59% on the base side) to bound its own noise.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: Support XQA backend for SpecDec verify
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Adds support for TRT-LLM XQA decode backend for SM90/120 speculative decoding, by building a causal mask it requires for the verify forward pass (more than 1 q token).

Agent generated summary:

Before: pure `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` + NEXTN on SM90/120 died at server startup during decode CUDA-graph capture — verify routes to the XQA decode kernel, which demands a mask for `q_len > 1` that the backend never passed:
```
  File "/SGL/flashinfer/flashinfer/xqa.py", line 332, in xqa                                                       
      assert mask is not None, "Mask is required for speculative decoding"                                         
  AssertionError: Mask is required for speculative decoding 
```

Never caught before because the verify→decode-kernel routing was written for SM100 (trtllm-gen needs no mask); XQA enablement for SM90/120 came later and nobody ran spec decoding on that combo.
                                                                                                                   

## Modifications

Fix/After: precompute XQA's bit-packed causal mask (constant for chain/topk=1 speculation) at init and pass it on verify — flashinfer already plumbed the argument. 

## Accuracy Tests

Validated: boots through capture, GPQA-10 0.70, acceptance 2.20/0.40 matching the FA3-verify reference (see MTP data reported in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23112).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.

title: [diffusion] Add native Anima Base v1.0 support
body:
## Summary

Add native text-to-image support for `circlestone-labs/Anima-Base-v1.0-Diffusers`.

- Implement Anima's Cosmos Predict2 transformer and learned T5-token conditioner with native attention, linear layers, TP/SP, and layerwise offload.
- Reuse the Qwen3 encoder, Qwen-Image VAE, component loaders, scheduler, denoising loop, and serving API. Read the official modular checkpoint layout without conversion or a Diffusers runtime upgrade.
- Integrate Cache-DiT and breakable CUDA graphs. Preserve the conditioner's unmasked padding semantics instead of adding graph-bucket padding.
- Add numerical/registration regressions, an opt-in repeated-request HTTP test, a nightly generation case, and a cookbook/deployment picker.

Scope is Base v1.0. Aesthetic/Turbo and single-file ComfyUI checkpoints are not covered. The cookbook links the checkpoint's non-commercial license.

## Validation

Remote validation on up to two H200 GPUs, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Diffusers 0.37.0, Transformers 5.12.1:

- 76 related unit tests and seven subtests passed, including full tiny-transformer FP32/BF16 comparisons against Diffusers Cosmos.
- The additional full `test_server_args.py` run plus Anima contracts had 213 passing tests and one LTX placement assertion failure (`test_auto_ltx_original_replaces_component_cpu_offload`). The same failure reproduces on the unchanged base `82cdd72588e4` source tree on H200; this PR does not change that policy.
- HTTP tests passed for 512px/4-step/two-output and 1024px/30-step/single-output requests, with two identical requests per case and pixel-exact repeatability.
- Full-checkpoint functional checks passed for TP2, Ulysses2, Ring2+FA, CFG2, encoder folding, DiT/conditioner layerwise offload, parallel tiled VAE decode, FA/SDPA, SageAttention (pinned SM90 build), Cache-DiT (30 steps), and actual breakable graph capture/replay. Sage and Cache-DiT are approximate paths, not quality-equivalent replacements.
- At 512px/30 steps, CFG 4, seed 42, CPU generator, BF16 components, FP32 latents, and matched SDPA, native versus official Diffusers output measured SSIM **0.9512**, PSNR **31.61 dB**. First positive/negative DiT noise-prediction cosine similarity was **0.999991/0.999992**. This is one sample, not a general quality guarantee or a speedup claim.

The reference uses Diffusers commit `0377f0c1b34e3ff313d41edad1bd79c2ed8bb5ec` in a separate environment. Tests do not claim coverage of TPxSP combinations, multi-node execution, non-NVIDIA hardware, or third-party LoRAs. No H100 performance baseline or consistency GT is fabricated from the H200 measurements.

Desktop validation also passed on RTX 5090 (32 GB VRAM, x86_64) and DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB unified memory, ARM64), using the same package versions above and source `7f3f903f039`. Both used one GPU, `--performance-mode speed --attention-backend torch_sdpa`, with no CPU offload. Each completed two 1024px/30-step/single-output HTTP requests and two 512px/4-step/two-output requests; corresponding same-device repeats were pixel-exact, and output images were visually inspected. These are functional checks, not throughput benchmarks or cross-hardware bitwise-equivalence claims. The cookbook now defaults to RTX 5090 and marks only the tested recipes verified; Anima-specific compatibility details live in the cookbook rather than the shared compatibility matrix.

## Measured Deployment Recipes

The cookbook now selects measured recipes rather than functional-only baselines. At 1024x1024, 30 steps, CFG 4, n=1, CPU generator and PNG/base64 output, five warm sequential HTTP requests gave:

| Hardware | Original eager | Recommended | Configuration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 5090 32 GB | 6.99 s | 6.10 s | cuDNN SDPA + compile, tiled VAE |
| DGX Spark 128 GB unified | 26.03 s | 17.41 s | Torch SDPA + compile, tiled VAE |
| H200 141 GB | 3.22 s | 2.22 s | FA + compile, untiled VAE |

Two NVLink H200s with CFG parallelism + compile + untiled VAE measured 1.28 s. Untiled H200 recipes use about 4-5 GiB more allocated memory and are verified only at 1024/n1. Tiled paths also passed 512/n1, 1024/n2, and 1536/n1. At 512, CFG eager beat compiled; TP2/SP2 compilation was not the winner.

This search included 418 timed HTTP requests across 96 completed workload/configuration combinations. Startup/compilation time is excluded. The final recipes use default CPU-thread settings; no approximate caching or quantized attention is enabled. The three single-GPU recipes measured PSNR 21.95-35.44 dB / SSIM 0.851-0.969 against same-device eager across three prompt/seed pairs, not pixel equivalence or a perceptual quality guarantee.

Eager remains selectable. The picker only changes Anima recipes, not global runtime defaults. Pre-commit, cookbook config checks, Mintlify validation and browser interaction checks passed.

## Reproduce HTTP Tests

```bash
SGLANG_ANIMA_TEST_MODEL=circlestone-labs/Anima-Base-v1.0-Diffusers \
  python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_anima.py -q
```

title: [HiCache]: Fix host lock ownership across radix splits
body:
## Motivation

HiCache can corrupt a value being written to L3 storage when a radix-tree node is split while its write-back SET is still in flight.
The SET reads directly from host KV-cache blocks. A split creates a new prefix node for the shared tokens, but that fragment does not inherit the parent's full host lock. Duplicate-host reclamation may therefore free and reuse the prefix blocks before the storage backend has finished reading them, this causes **wrong data to be written to storage**. The backend behaves correctly: it stores exactly what is in those buffers when its SET runs. The stale write is caused by SGLang changing ownership of the buffers too early.

## Modifications

* Propagate a full host lock from the original node to the prefix fragment created by a split.
* When the asynchronous SET finishes, release the lock across every fragment created after the SET began, stopping at the recorded pre-split parent. 
* Require the acquisition result when releasing a host lock. Without its pre-split boundary, a parameterless release could unlock only the original child and permanently leak the copied prefix lock.
* Apply the same ownership rule to the Python and Rust unified radix-tree implementations.

This keeps every zero-copy SET source block owned by the SET until the backend call has returned, even if the radix node is split in the meantime.


## Accuracy Tests

I tested this with both unit tests (in this PR) an [end2end reproducer (not in this PR)](https://github.com/lluki/sglang/blob/751ee8dd1656f365ba555267fd706dc054ef3d97/scripts/repro_hicache_nixl_stale_set_frontend.py). 

The e2e verifier runs SGLang with hicache nixl backend and slows down the `batch_set_*` artificially to reliably trigger the bug:
* Send an 832-token victim prompt whose deterministic answer is ZEBRA4821.
* Send a 3500-token unrelated prompt. This evicts the victim to host and starts its delayed POSIX SET.
* Send a prompt that shares the first 704 victim tokens and then diverges.
* This splits the host-backed node while its SET is in flight.
* Send a 3000-token unrelated prompt to create host pressure. On buggy code, the split prefix is reclaimed and its host blocks are reused.
* Wait for the SET, flush the memory tiers, and send the original victim completion request again so it must be loaded from POSIX storage.

The second request reports a 768-token storage hit, proving that it exercised L3. On buggy upstream code its answer changes from ZEBRA4821 to repeated Answer: tokens. This is visible entirely through the completion API.

I ran this validation and testsuite with both python and rust cores.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A

title: fix: load fused shared-expert LoRA weights and bound expert indices
body:
Fix fused shared-expert LoRA loading and prevent expert IDs from aliasing another adapter.

- Size each layer's LoRA expert pool from its actual fused MoE layout, including shared slots.
- Load shared-expert factors into those slots using the base module's EP mapping and existing TP slicing/scaling; merge packed routed factors regardless of checkpoint key order.
- Assert while allocating the pool that both A/B expert dimensions match the base fused MoE layout (local or global IDs); no device assert or GPU synchronization.
- Reject unsupported shared-outer factors and global-ID/per-rank shared-slot layouts; reject out-of-range expert IDs before adding adapter offsets.

Selected for the v0.1.1 cutoff. FP32 Qwen3-MoE router support remains after cutoff in #40997, paired with Miles #3697. No dtype or accumulation-policy change. 

Validation: existing coverage includes 60 passing tests (5 abstract-base skips), a distinguishing GPU bounds regression, and GLM-5.2 5L TP4/EP1 with fusion enabled. On 8 DAPO 4K sequences ×3, the shared-expert fix reduced slot mean logprob differences from 0.050144/0.039706 to 0.019414/0.015895 (base 0.013156); the additional Bridge row-parallel fix is separate and is not part of this cutoff PR. EP mapping is unit-tested; distributed EP, other backends and CUDA-graph combinations are not comprehensively validated. A host-only probe of the actual initialization check accepts matching global/local dimensions and rejects a missing shared slot on either A or B. CPU loader regression: packed-first and shared-first inputs failed in all 6 EP/order subcases before the fix; after merging packed routed views with shared factors, the full loader file passes 46 tests and 13 subtests. Test fixture cleanup removes 45 net lines. Full local pre-commit passed; fresh split-head GPU CI is pending.

title: [AMD][Qwen3-Next] Consume the AITER fused GDN prefill kernel
body:
## [Qwen3-Next] Consume the AITER fused GDN prefill kernel

### Motivation
The Qwen3-Next GDN (gated delta-net) **prefill** runs as a four-kernel chain today
(`causal_conv1d_split_qkv` → fused gating → the fp32 chunked delta-rule scan →
gated RMSNorm), so the large intermediate tensors round-trip through HBM between
each launch. AITER now ships a **fused single-kernel prefill**
(`fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz`, ROCm/aiter#5606) that folds that chain into a tight set
of Gluon launches and emits the per-head group-128 FP8 activations a block-FP8
`out_proj` consumes directly.

This PR wires sglang to use it. It is the **prefill sibling of #39554** (the decode
consumer of ROCm/aiter#5520) and shares the same opt-in switch, so one flag enables
both phases:

```
SGLANG_QWEN3_NEXT_GDN_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter
```

Off by default. Everything is probed, nothing assumed — unsupported platform,
older Triton, or an uncovered call runs the existing unfused chain unchanged.

### What it does
- **Adapter** `kernels/ops/attention/gdn_fused_prefill_aiter.py` — fail-closed
  `available()` / `covered()` / `run()`: platform, opt-in env, a Triton ≥ 3.8 Gluon
  probe, and a per-call shape/dtype contract delegated to AITER's own predicate so
  the two can't drift.
- **`GDNAttnBackend.try_fused_gdn_prefill`** — builds the ragged-batch args
  (`cu_seqlens` from `query_start_loc`, `has_initial_state` from `extend_prefix_lens`,
  `cache_indices` from the mamba pool) and the conv/state pools, calls
  `covered() → run()`, and stashes the post-norm output + group-128 FP8 activations.
  Declines MIS / target-verify / tracked-conv batches.
- **`RadixLinearAttention.try_fused_gdn_prefill`** — unwraps `HybridLinearAttnBackend`
  to reach the GDN backend; guards extend / not-verify / not-piecewise.
- **`qwen3_next.py`** — static readiness gate (`available()` + `num_v_heads ==
  2·num_k_heads` + `head_k == head_v == 128` + `conv == 4`), publishes the bf16 norm
  weight after load, attempts the fused path first in `forward`; when `out_proj` is
  block-FP8 it feeds the kernel's group-128 FP8 activations straight in (no re-quant),
  else the bf16 normalized output.

### Files changed (4 files)
| File | + | What |
|------|---|------|
| `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/gdn_fused_prefill_aiter.py` | 165 (new) | Fail-closed adapter (available/covered/run) |
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py` | 76 | `try_fused_gdn_prefill` dispatch + stash |
| `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_next.py` | 82 | readiness gate, norm-weight publish, attempt-first + block-FP8 out_proj feed |
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_linear_attention.py` | 45 | backend unwrap + guards |

### Dependency
Requires the AITER fused prefill kernel **ROCm/aiter#5606**. Fail-closed, so this
merges safely before that lands — the fused path simply activates once the kernel
is importable.

### Accuracy — run command
Same model/args with the flag on vs off; GSM8K must stay at parity. Needs a
gfx950 (MI350-series) host with Triton ≥ 3.8.

```bash
# fused ON (add the flag) vs OFF (drop it); TP4, Qwen3-Next-80B FP8
SGLANG_QWEN3_NEXT_GDN_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8> \
  --tp-size 4 --quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --attention-backend aiter --context-length 8192 &

python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 32 --port 30000
```
Result (MI355X): **GSM8K parity** — fused 0.953 vs stock 0.950.

### Perf
End-to-end A/B, flag on vs off, same Triton-3.8 image (isolates the kernel), TP4,
Qwen3-Next-80B FP8, MI355X.

**Prefill-focused (ISL 6144 / OSL 8):**

| metric | stock | fused | Δ |
|--------|------:|------:|---|
| Median TTFT (ms) | 647.9 | 471.6 | **−27%** |
| Input throughput (tok/s) | 92.8k | 125.4k | **+35%** |

**Balanced 1k/1k, concurrency sweep (Median TTFT, ms):**

| conc | stock | fused | Δ |
|-----:|------:|------:|---|
| 1  | 69.8  | 61.1  | −12% |
| 4  | 137.2 | 115.4 | −16% |
| 8  | 141.4 | 138.9 | −2%  |
| 16 | 205.9 | 193.3 | −6%  |
| 32 | 356.3 | 339.5 | −5%  |

TPOT is identical on both arms (decode path untouched); the win is prefill-side,
largest where prefill is a bigger fraction of the request (low concurrency / long
prompts) and diluting as the decode-heavy steady state dominates.

title: [CPU][kernel] fix rope for VLA model on CPU
body:
## Motivation
`torch.ops.sgl_kernel.apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu` kernel only takes 3D `[num_tokens, num_heads, head_size]` inputs and had no `unsqueeze_dim` argument. Pi0.5 calls it with 4D `[batch, num_heads, seq_len, head_size]` q/k and `unsqueeze_dim=1`, so it failed on CPU:

```
"/python/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vlas/pi05_core.py", line 382, in forward
    query_states, key_states = native_apply_rotary_pos_emb(
  File "//lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/_ops.py", line 1350, in __call__
    return self._op(*args, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: sgl_kernel::apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu() expected at most 4 argument(s) but received 5 argument(s). Declaration: sgl_kernel::apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu(Tensor query, Tensor key, Tensor cos, Tensor sin) -> (Tensor, Tensor)
```
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vlas/pi05_core.py#L902C32-L902C59

## Modifications

- `apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu` now takes `unsqueeze_dim` (default 1) and supports q/k of 3D and higher, with the head dim at `unsqueeze_dim` (e.g. `[B, H, S, D]` or `[B, S, H, D]`). It is out-of-place, matching `apply_rotary_pos_emb_native`.
- The neox rope path now handles float32 inputs, and the CPU graph fake op is updated for the new signature.

## Test Coverage

- pi0.5 model functionality

- `test_apply_rotary_pos_emb` in `test/registered/cpu/test_rope.py`. It compares against the native reference for:
  (1) 3D with GQA, 4D `[B, H, S, D]` with `unsqueeze_dim=1`, and (2) 4D `[B, S, H, D]` with `unsqueeze_dim=2`

title: [Fix] Stop counting a deferred FFN sum more than once: replicated TP1 shared expert, dense reduce_scatterv
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* __->__ #41195
* #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

This PR fixes two cases where a layer's output was summed more than it should be when its FFN reduction runs later than the FFN.

1. **Replicated TP1 shared expert.** With `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1`, Laguna and `DeepseekV2MoE` (DeepSeek-V2/V3, GLM5-Next without MHC) replicate the shared expert on every TP rank and add its full output after the MoE all-reduce. When that all-reduce is left to a later step, the MoE block returns a partial sum and every rank still adds the shared output. So the later sum counts it `tp_size` times. The later step is either fused into the next layer's residual norm, or, under DP attention, the reduce-scatter back to the local tokens.
2. **Dense layers under DP attention reduce_scatterv.** Under DP attention with tp == dp == ep and no a2a backend, `postprocess_layer` reduce-scatterv'd every FULL-mode layer's output, whether or not the layer allows reduce-scatter.
   - A MoE block leaves its all-reduce out under the same condition, so that sum is owed.
   - A dense MLP leaves it out only under the published `mlp_reduce_scatter`, which needs `allow_reduce_scatter`. Without it, the MLP has already all-reduced, and the reduce-scatterv sums the output `tp_size` times.

   The layers affected are the dense layers of Qwen3, MOSS-VL, Step3-VL, LongCat-Flash and Bailing-MoE-Linear, and the MiMo-V2 MTP layer. The MoE blocks of Step3-VL (`Step3TextMoEMLP`) and LongCat-Flash (`LongcatFlashMoE`) all-reduce inside the block, so reduce_scatterv still sums their output twice; this PR does not change them. Separately, the LongCat-Flash NextN dense MLP never reduced its output at TP > 1; only reduce_scatterv summed it, by accident.

## Modifications

- **TP1 shared expert:**
  - `should_add_replicated_moe_output()`: when a later step still owes the TP sum, only TP rank 0 adds the replicated shared output; otherwise every rank adds it. Paths that reduce inside the MoE block, or whose output is already complete, keep their numerics.
  - A source guard requires every model that reads `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1` to add the shared output under this predicate.
- **Dense reduce_scatterv:**
  - postprocess uses reduce_scatterv only when the layer is sparse or allows reduce-scatter, and otherwise scatters without summing. `LayerScatterModes` records `is_layer_sparse` for this.
  - The LongCat-Flash NextN MLP all-reduces its own output like the other dense layers.
  - `test_postprocess_reduce_scatterv.py` pairs every (sparse × allow) combination with the FFN's own skip predicate, so postprocess sums exactly when the FFN left the sum out.

## Accuracy Tests

**TP1 shared expert, B200, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 with the env on** (4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared; TP1 is the reference):

| Config | First diverging token (4 requests) | Max step-0 top-5 \|Δlogp\| |
|---|---|---|
| parent, fusion on | 1, 1, 1, 0 | 1.846 |
| this PR, fusion on | 32, 4, 32, 32 | 0.112 |
| parent, fusion off (noise reference) | 1, 32, 32, 32 | 0.092 |
| parent, DP attention (dp 2) | 1, 1, 1, 2 | 1.075 |
| this PR, DP attention (dp 2) | 32, 32, 32, 32 | 0.073 |

The configurations that owe no later sum are bit-identical to the parent: env on with fusion off, and env off with fusion on.

**Dense reduce_scatterv, B200:**

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| main, Qwen3-0.6B TP2 DP2 ep 2 | diverges at tokens 0, 0, 6, 1 (max step-0 top-5 \|Δlogp\| 1.75); output turns into garbage |
| main, same with ep 1 (reduce_scatterv does not apply) | TP2 noise level |
| this PR, ep 2 vs this PR, ep 1 | identical (for a dense model, ep only changes the reduce_scatterv decision) |
| this PR ep 1 vs main ep 1 | identical |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 DP2 ep 2 (sparse, allows reduce-scatter), parent vs this PR | identical |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 DP2 ep 2, parent vs this PR | identical |

The unit tests for MoE output reduction, the layer-stack exit, aux capture, postprocess reduce_scatterv, the layout and the CP dense MLP all pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No collective is added. The dense reduce_scatterv fix replaces a reduce-scatter with a scatter on the affected layers.

title: [Refactor] Take a layer's last-layer fact from its scatter-mode plan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* __->__ #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* #41195
* #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

Each model passed `LayerCommunicator` an `is_last_layer` expression next to the `LayerScatterModes.init_new(layer_id, num_layers)` call. That call already decides the same fact: the plan's last layer returns the model's output layout. The two expressions were written separately in every model, and three NextN / MTP draft layers had them disagree (fixed earlier in this stack).

## Modifications

- **`LayerScatterModes`:** carries `is_last_layer`, computed from the condition its layout plan uses (`layer_id == num_layers - 1`).
- **`LayerCommunicator`:** reads it from there and no longer takes an argument.
- **22 model files:** drop the `is_last_layer=` argument. `bailing_moe.py` also drops an attribute that only fed it; `llada2.py`'s `is_last_layer` and `gpt_oss.py`'s `is_nextn`, which nothing reads any more, go too.
- **Nemotron-H:** it builds its `LayerScatterModes` directly, so it hands its last layer to that builder. The MTP layer still sets its communicator's `is_last_layer = True` after construction, as before, so there the communicator and the plan disagree; nothing reads the plan's copy on that layer.
- **LayerNorm SP sibling:** copies the fact with the plan.
- **MHC and DSA-CP communicators:** drop the argument.
- **`test_last_layer_communicator.py`:** reads the plan and checks that models no longer pass the fact; a new case checks `init_new` itself.

The models that passed nothing before now get `True` on their last layer, but they read it nowhere. They make no FFN-exit decision, and their reduce-scatter decision reads it only on the input-scattered path, which they never enter.

## Accuracy Tests

No behavior change.

- **AST check:** removing the `is_last_layer` keyword from the parent's 22 model files gives exactly the new files.
- **CPU unit battery (unit/models + unit/layers):** results per file match the parent when each file runs on its own.
- **GPU, B200, fusion on, 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared:** Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2, GLM-4.7-Flash TP2, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 × DP2 and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B TP2 are all bit-identical to the parent. The per-layer FFN-exit audit is identical: a layer whose last-layer fact flipped would change its fuse / defer decision.

No runtime change.

title: [Fix] Plan NextN / MTP draft layers as one-layer models and fix the Bailing V2 NextN draft
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* #41195
* __->__ #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

This PR fixes three defects in NextN / MTP draft layers. Each commit fixes one.

1. **Layout plan.** `LayerScatterModes` treats `layer_id == 0` as the first layer (it takes the model's input layout) and `layer_id == num_layers - 1` as the last (it returns the model's output layout). Two draft layers were planned as middle layers instead:
   - the Bailing V2 / V2.5 NextN layers, passed as layer 0 of `num_hidden_layers`;
   - the Step-3.5 MTP layer, passed as layer 45 of 1.

   When the draft's MLP runs on SCATTERED tokens with attention TP > 1, the draft returned this rank's shard of tokens to the logits and to the next step. The SCATTERED triggers are an a2a backend, dwdp, FP4 cutlass allgather, or `moe_dense_tp_size` 1. The Step-3.5 MTP layer also planned an all-gather for an input that is already full. Separately, the Bailing V2.5 NextN plan treated the layer as dense whenever the model's first layers are dense, even though the layer builds an MoE. DeepSeek NextN and Bailing V3 already pass layer 0 of 1 (the same fix as #7420 for DeepSeek).
2. **Unloaded Bailing V2 NextN MLP.** `BailingMoEBlock` chose between the MoE and the dense MLP with `is_nextn=False`. So the NextN layer (layer 0) became a dense MLP whenever `first_k_dense_replace >= 1`, while the checkpoint's NextN layer holds expert weights (Ling-mini-2.0: `model.layers.20.mlp.experts.*`). `load_weights` skips names with no matching parameter, so the draft ran an MLP whose weights were never loaded (all zeros).
3. **Bailing V2 NextN could not start.** Every Bailing draft is renamed `BailingMoeForCausalLMNextN`, and `_derive_model_shapes` sent that name down the MLA branch added for V2.5. V2 is GQA and has no `kv_lora_rank`, so NextN speculative decoding on a V2 target failed at startup with `'BailingMoeV2Config' object has no attribute 'kv_lora_rank'`.

## Modifications

- **`models/bailing_moe.py`, `models/bailing_moe_linear.py`, `models/step3p5.py`:** draft layers pass `layer_id=0, num_layers=1` to `LayerScatterModes.init_new`. The Step-3.5 layer id still indexes its per-layer config. The Bailing V2.5 NextN plan is sparse.
- **`models/bailing_moe.py`:** the NextN layer builds `BailingMoESparseMoeBlock`.
- **`configs/model_config.py`:** the MLA branch takes `BailingMoeForCausalLMNextN` only when the draft config carries `kv_lora_rank`, which the V2.5 and V3 drafts do. A V2 draft now derives its shapes the way its target does. V3 drafts still take this branch rather than the V3 one, as before.
- **Tests:**
  - `test_last_layer_communicator.py` now records the `LayerScatterModes.init_new` arguments. It checks that every draft layer is planned as layer 0 of 1, that the V2.5 NextN plan is sparse, and that the V2 NextN layer builds the MoE block.
  - `test_model_config_shapes.py`: a GQA and an MLA Bailing draft each keep their attention architecture.

  All of these fail on main.

Configurations whose MLP does not run on SCATTERED tokens plan the same layouts before and after.

## Accuracy Tests

**GPU, H200, Ling-mini-base-2.0 TP2.** 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared. NextN speculative decoding with 1 step, topk 1 and 2 draft tokens; also the default 3 / 1 / 4. Accept length = completion tokens / verify steps.

Runs before the third commit need a test-harness shim that only derives the draft's shapes. It is applied identically to every tree and is not needed after the third commit.

| Tree | Config | Result | Accept length |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | speculative off | reference | – |
| main / first commit | speculative | identical to the reference | 1.600 / 1.600 |
| second commit | speculative | text identical to the reference | **1.939** |
| main / first / second | speculative, default 3 / 1 / 4 | text identical | 1.684 / 1.684 / **2.462** |
| main | speculative, `moe_dense_tp_size=1` | **crash** on the first draft forward: index out of bounds in `logits_processor._get_logits` | – |
| first / second commit | speculative, `moe_dense_tp_size=1` | identical to the target-only run with the same setting | 1.580 / 1.910 |
| third commit, no shim | the configurations above | starts; identical to each shimmed run | 1.939 / 2.462 / 1.910 |

- **Draft-layer audit:**
  - main under `moe_dense_tp_size=1`: `mlp=SCATTERED, layer_output_mode=SCATTERED`;
  - first commit: `layer_output_mode=TP_ATTN_FULL`;
  - second commit: the NextN layer is `BailingMoESparseMoeBlock`.
- **Weight checksums before and after `load_weights`:**
  - on main, the draft's dense `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj` stay all zeros;
  - after the second commit, only the `word_embeddings` / `lm_head` shared with the target are untouched.

**GPU, H200, Step-3.5-Flash BF16 TP8 MTP** (EAGLE 3 / 1 / 4):

- **Default configuration:** main and this PR are bit-identical (accept length 2.560).
- **With `moe_dense_tp_size=1`:** main crashes in the draft's CUDA graph capture (`size of tensor a (32) must match ... b (4)`: the MTP layer returned its shard), and this PR does not.
- **Caveat:** the Step-3.5 target and its MTP draft are not correct under that setting. `Step3p5MLP` always shards over TP and all-reduces, so on SCATTERED tokens it sums different ranks' tokens. Only the crash fix is verified here, not end-to-end output; the dense MLP under `moe_dense_tp_size=1` is left for a follow-up.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The layout plans change only under the SCATTERED triggers, and the second commit makes the draft's MLP the MoE the checkpoint was trained with.

title: [Refactor] Leave the FFN reduction to the next layer under attention DP
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* __->__ #41197
* #41196
* #41195
* #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

Under attention DP, `postprocess_layer` brings a FULL-layout layer output back to this rank's tokens. It does so in one of two ways:

- **FFN left its sum out:** a reduce-scatter (reduce_scatterv, or `dp_reduce_scatter_tensor` on MAX_LEN padding) that also completes the sum;
- **FFN reduced its own output:** a plain scatter.

Both ran in the layer, while without attention DP the next layer's input already completes a deferred sum. This PR moves both to the next layer's input, so a layer's FFN sum is always completed where the next layer reads it.

## Modifications

- **First commit:**
  - Postprocess's `_scatter_hidden_states` is split into `_reduce_and_redistribute_output_varlen`, `_reduce_and_redistribute_output_max_len` and `_redistribute_output`, chosen under the same conditions as before.
  - `FfnExit.finish` returns `UnreducedOutput(partial, reduce_and_redistribute=...)` when postprocess would run one of the reduce-scatters. This applies on a FULL → TP_ATTN_FULL layer that is not the last one and is not in an active LayerNorm SP region.
  - `prepare_attn` runs the bound reduce-scatter first, where postprocess used to, then takes the complete-input path. No fused kernel runs under attention DP.
- **Second commit:**
  - `should_defer_ffn_reduction` also defers under attention DP when postprocess would only scatter: the next layer runs the FFN's all-reduce and then the scatter.
  - The token check reads the gathered buffer length under attention DP, so every DP rank takes the same decision on the new deferral. The fused decision (`should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer`) still reads the local batch size; that is harmless because neither fused kernel runs under attention DP.
  - A guard, `TestFfnExitUsersOweATpSum`, walks from every `ffn_exit` caller through its FFN parts. It checks that none of them sums only over the attention-TP group (`use_dp_attention_reduce`), because the next layer completes a TP-group sum.

- **Layer-input buffer:** under attention DP, `layer_input_buffer()` in DeepSeek and GLM5-Next now yields the previous layer's FULL-length partial. The non-inplace flashinfer TRT-LLM MoE's `moe_output_buffer` check then matches its shape, and the MoE writes its output into that tensor. The partial is dead once `prepare_attn` has reduced it.
- **Two-batch overlap:** the layer before a TBO section can now hand the TBO entry an `UnreducedOutput` under attention DP. The entry reduces it first; that fix lives in #41196, where the same read was already reachable.

## Accuracy Tests

No numeric change: the same collectives run on the same tensors, one layer boundary later.

- **Call sequences** (stubbed collectives):
  - boundary-level, 8,192 cases: identical to the parent;
  - end to end (the FFN exit's real decision and the FFN's own skip rule), 4,096 cases: identical;
  - `prepare_attn`, 24,576 cases: identical.

title: [Refactor] Build prepare_mlp and the layout moves from named steps
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* __->__ #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* #41195
* #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

`CommunicateWithAllReduceAndLayerNormFn._gather_hidden_states_and_residual`, the boundary from the attention output to the FFN input, wrote its three orders inline:

- without attention DP;
- the attention-DP replicate order;
- the attention-DP partial order.

Each order mixed the collectives, the residual add and the norm with the fusion, quantization and platform branches. The postprocess functions and the `prepare_mlp` paths to SCATTERED and to the MoE context-parallel group also wrote their token moves inline, and `_scatter_hidden_states_moe` repeated the DP scatter that `_scatter_hidden_states` already has.

This PR builds these boundaries from named steps, the same way #41084 split `prepare_attn`. It also rejects one input that `prepare_attn` would have computed wrongly.

## Modifications

All in `layers/communicator.py`.

- **`_gather_hidden_states_and_residual`** is now a sequence of steps:
  - **Without attention DP:** it tries the fused kernel first, `_mlp_input_reduce_output_and_update_and_read_residual()` (all-reduce, residual add and norm together; returns None when no kernel takes the batch). Otherwise it runs `_mlp_input_reduce_output()` (the attention-TP all-reduce, quantized outside decode when quantized communication is on), then the NPU weight prefetch, then the norm.
  - **Attention DP, replicate order:** attention-TP all-reduce, then the norm under symmetric memory, then `_redistribute_input_to_dp()`.
  - **Attention DP, partial order:** attention-TP rank 0 adds the residual, then `_reduce_and_redistribute_output_to_dp()`, then `dp_scatter` back into the residual, then the norm on the gathered tokens.
  - **Scattered residual:** a residual scattered over attention TP is gathered first with `_redistribute_from_attn_tp_shards()`.
  - **Function identity:** the function object is unchanged, so the MHC and DSA-CP mappings, `_post_attn_residual_is_read_only` and the CuteDSL eligibility check that identify it keep working.
- **Layout moves:**
  - **`prepare_mlp` to SCATTERED** (`_scatter_hidden_states_and_residual`): `_reduce_and_redistribute_output_to_attn_tp_shards()`, then `_redistribute_to_attn_tp_shards()`, then the norm.
  - **`prepare_mlp` to MOE_FULL:** the padded MoE-CP all-gather is now `_redistribute_input_to_moe_cp()`.
  - **Postprocess `_scatter_hidden_states_moe`:** it takes this CP rank's tokens back with `_redistribute_output_from_moe_cp()`. Under attention DP it scatters to this rank's tokens through the same `_to_local_tokens` / `_redistribute_output` path as `_scatter_hidden_states`, and no longer repeats the group choice and `dp_scatter`.
  - **Postprocess `_gather`:** it adds the residual and gathers with `_redistribute_from_attn_tp_shards()`. `_scatter` takes this rank's shard with `_redistribute_to_attn_tp_shards()`. The single-tensor case of `CommunicateSimpleFn._scattered_to_tp_attn_full` calls `_redistribute_from_attn_tp_shards()` too, instead of repeating the same two calls.
- **`prepare_attn`** now raises when it receives an `UnreducedOutput` without a residual. Before, a plain one would have been normalized as if its sum were complete, and one that also moves tokens would have been completed and then lost the residual stream. No producer hands one over today. `test_prepare_attn_steps.py` covers the new check.

## Accuracy Tests

No behavior change is expected. The checks below replace every collective, kernel, buffer and platform flag with recording stubs and compare against the parent commit.

- **`_gather_hidden_states_and_residual`, 24,576 cases:** same calls, arguments and returned objects in every case.
  - **Matrix:** attention DP × attention TP × rank × `force_layernorm_before_dp_gather` × scattered residual × input-scattered × empty batch × fusion (none / aiter / FlashInfer) × norm fusion support × quantized communication × decode × NPU × weight cache × symmetric memory.
  - **Paths reached:** no DP 14,592, quantized 1,024, fused 2,048, DP replicate 4,608, DP partial 1,536, input-scattered 768.
- **Layout moves, 30,720 cases** over the five functions. Tensors are tagged with their shape and value sum, so a different slice, in-place add or buffer would show up.
  - The 20,160 cases that run are identical.
  - 768 cases differ only in the error text (`list` vs `tuple` index). All of them are the impossible configuration attention-TP rank 1 with attention-TP size 1.
- **`prepare_attn`, 24,576 cases:** identical, except the 6,144 cases with a pending sum and no residual. Those now raise before making any call.
- **Unit tests:** the files that exercise these functions pass: layout, FFN exit, fusion gate, LayerNorm SP, reduce-scatterv, LongCat shortcut, CP dense MLP, and the `prepare_attn` steps.

Bit-identical to the parent on B200 (4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared), covering each `prepare_mlp` order:

- **Without attention DP:** Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 with fusion on (fused path) and off (unfused path); GLM-4.7-Flash TP2.
- **Attention DP, replicate order:** DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 × DP2 (attention TP 1).
- **Attention DP, partial order:** Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP4 × DP2 × EP2 and DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP4 × DP2 (attention TP 2).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. Eager mode adds a few Python calls per boundary; no kernel or collective changes.

title: [Refactor] Decide an FFN exit's completion once and declare the group it owes
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* #41195
* #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

- **Decided twice.** `FfnExit` asked three decisions before the FFN ran. Then `finish()` chose again how the next layer completes the output (`_scatter_for_next_layer`, `_reduce_scatter_for_next_layer`), reading the postprocess function's identity and comparing step objects.
- **Group guessed by the consumer.** The next layer completed a deferred sum with `deferred_post_experts_all_reduce`, which picks the MoE output's group, even for a dense layer.

## Modifications

- **`LayerCommunicator._select_ffn_completion`:** decides once, before the FFN runs, what the FFN skips (the published flags) and what completes its output: the next layer's input, or this layer's postprocess. `FfnExit.finish` only wraps the output or runs postprocess.
- **`UnreducedOutput` carries the group its partial owes one all-reduce over,** declared by the producer:
  - the TP group for a dense layer;
  - the MoE output's group for a sparse one.

  `post_experts_reduction_group` now defines that group once; `deferred_post_experts_all_reduce` and `resolve_fusion_group` use it. `reduce_output` and `prepare_attn`'s unfused completion all-reduce over the declared group. `prepare_attn` hands the partial to the fused kernel, which reduces over the MoE output's group, only when that is the declared group.
- **Postprocess capability at construction:** whether postprocess's move back to this rank's tokens can run in the next layer is fixed once. It is true for the base `_scatter_hidden_states`, not for the MHC or DSA-CP ones.
- **Reduce-scatter step:** it returns None when only a scatter remains, instead of being compared with `_redistribute_output`.
- **Removed:** `_scatter_for_next_layer`, `_reduce_scatter_for_next_layer`, `_next_layer_input_can_restore_the_layout` and `_output_to_local_tokens_step`.
- **Nemotron-H:** its deferred outputs declare the same groups: the TP group for a Mamba or attention output, and the communicator's `ffn_reduction_group()` for an MLP or MoE output.

**Incidental fix.** The declared group follows what the FFN owes. It differs from the MoE rule only when the MoE group is not the TP group. That needs `moe_dp_size > 1`, which in turn requires context parallel. There, a dense layer's deferred sum was completed over the EP group only; it is now completed over the TP group, fused or not (the fused kernel is skipped, since it reduces over the EP group). No supported configuration reaches this today: the prefill context-parallel modes either force DP attention and `moe_dense_tp_size=1`, or plan dense layers as MOE_FULL.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Decision-table call sequences, 46,080 cases.** Both trees run their own completion code, with `get_parallel` patched to recording groups in every module that reads it, so each all-reduce is recorded with its group object.
  - **Matrix:** attention DP on / off × fused kernel × group layout (pure TP / pure EP / mergeable EP × TP / EP group ≠ TP group) × dense / sparse × last layer × postprocess function × each excluded condition (a2a, complete output, quantized communication, TP1 shared, LoRA) × LayerNorm SP × reduce_scatterv / MAX_LEN / tiles × allow reduce-scatter × token counts × a reader between layers.
  - **Result:** 45,864 cases are identical. The other 216 are exactly the dense layer + fused decision + (EP group ≠ TP group) cases above, where the completion moves from the EP group to the TP group.
- **`prepare_attn` call sequences, 49,152 cases** (the previous matrix × whether the declared group is the fused kernel's): identical to the parent whenever it is. When it is not, the 1,536 cases with a pending sum, a residual and no post-residual addition no longer try the fused kernel and complete the sum unfused.
- **Unit tests:** the related files pass, including a new `prepare_attn` case for a partial owed over another group than the kernel's.
- **GPU, B200, fusion on, 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared:** Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2, GLM-4.7-Flash TP2, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B TP2 and DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 × DP2 (reduce-scatter and all-reduce + scatter moved to the next layer) are all bit-identical to the parent.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel or collective changes; the selection runs once per FFN instead of twice.

title: [Refactor] Move Step-3.5, GLM5-Next, Dots3, MiniMax-M3 and Qwen3.5 onto ffn_exit
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* __->__ #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* #41195
* #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

Step-3.5, GLM5-Next, Dots3, MiniMax-M3 and Qwen3.5 decided by hand whether to leave their FFN all-reduce to the next layer, from `should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer`. They published the flags themselves, then wrapped the output or ran postprocess. Moving them onto `ffn_exit` puts their decision in one place with the other layer-communicator models. They also gain the deferrals the previous PRs added (without the fused kernel, and under attention DP).

## Modifications

One commit per model:

- **Step-3.5:** the MoE layers use `ffn_exit`. The MoE still skips its internal all-reduce, so one all-reduce covers the MoE and shared-expert outputs. The dense layers keep reducing their own output.
- **GLM5-Next:** uses `ffn_exit`. The MHC layers never defer, as before.
- **Dots3:** uses `ffn_exit` and still passes the decisions to the MLP / MoE as arguments. Inside `ffn_exit` the same decisions are published, so the row-parallel layers agree with the arguments.
- **MiniMax-M3:** uses `ffn_exit`, and drops the forced in-layer all-reduce of sparse layers at TP > 1. It worked around a runaway without EOS, which came from the last layer's deferred sum reaching the final norm unreduced. #40868 fixed that, and the layer-stack exit now completes any sum the last layer leaves. This is a behavior change: with the fused kernel on, sparse layers now fuse like the dense ones.
- **Qwen3.5:** `FfnExit` decides the deferred MoE finalize and the reduction, and `FfnExit.finish` passes a handoff on, returns the unreduced output, or runs postprocess. The last-layer fallback is gone, and `_finish_mlp_output` is removed. The MoE block takes `ffn_exit.defer_moe_finalize` as is: the old check that the MLP input is a tensor is dropped, because `prepare_mlp` always returns one here.

## Accuracy Tests

4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared, decode CUDA graph on.

- **Step-3.5-Flash BF16 TP8, H200:** fusion on, fusion off, DP8 and DP2 are all bit-identical to the parent. The audit shows the new deferrals (fusion off: unfused deferral; DP: reduce-scatter moved).
- **Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 TP2, H200:** fusion on, fusion off, DP2, and DP2 with a ~3000-token prompt are bit-identical.
- **MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 TP4, B200:**
  - **Fusion off:** bit-identical to the parent. A difference in one request came from the parent itself: a second parent run matches this PR's two runs exactly.
  - **Fusion on:** GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot) is 0.91 on the parent and 0.91 on this PR. Of 20 raw prompts with EOS honored, the parent runs all 20 to the 1024-token limit; this PR stops at EOS on 8, and no new runaway appears. So this shows the change is not worse, not that the runaway is gone: 12 of the 20 still run to the limit.
- **GLM5-Next and Dots3:** no checkpoint was available; CPU unit tests only. Both now take new collective paths (the deferral without the fused kernel, and under attention DP the reduce-scatter moved to the next layer), which are GPU-checked on the other models only.
- **torch.compile:** these models now also defer without the fused kernel, in prefill too, so the `tc_piecewise` prefill backend cannot trace them at TP > 1 (see #41196). A MiniMax-M3 multimodal launch selects that backend by default.
- **CPU unit tests:** CuteDSL fusion, the Qwen3.5 loaders and pipeline parallel, the FFN exit, the layer-stack exit, aux capture and deepstack all pass.

Not measured separately. The collectives are those of the previous PRs; MiniMax-M3's sparse layers now take the fused kernel when fusion is on.

title: [Refactor] Carry a deferred FFN all-reduce as UnreducedOutput and complete it in the next layer without the fused kernel
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* __->__ #41196
* #41195
* #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

A decoder layer can leave its FFN all-reduce to the next layer's input norm. Until now it did so only when the fused all-reduce + residual + norm kernel took the batch, and it marked the output tensor with a `_sglang_needs_allreduce_fusion` attribute.

- **The marker was easy to lose.** Slicing, views and copies drop the attribute, and code that reads the tensor never sees it. So a consumer between layers could use the partial sum as if it were complete; the pipeline send, deepstack and aux capture fixes were each such a consumer.
- **The completion lived in two places.** The FFN reduced its own output whenever the fused kernel did not take the batch.

## Modifications

- **`UnreducedOutput`** (first commit): a small value holding the partial sum. It is not a tensor, so using it as one raises. Only the next layer's `prepare_attn` and an explicit `reduce_output()` read it.
  - `reduce_output()` replaces `complete_deferred_allreduce()`.
  - `layer_input_buffer()` serves the two layers that reuse their input's memory as the MoE output buffer.
  - `FfnExit.finish` returns the wrapper, and `finish_layer_stack` reduces it.
  - The CuteDSL communicator fuses the all-reduce of the wrapper's partial sum where it fused a marked tensor.
  - The models that set the marker themselves (Step-3.5, Qwen3.5, MiniMax-M3, GLM5-Next, Dots3, Nemotron-H) return the wrapper.
  - The deepstack additions and aux captures call `reduce_output()`. The two-batch-overlap entry reduces its input first, before it splits the batch and reads the input's length.
- **Next layer completes the sum** (second commit): `should_defer_ffn_reduction()`, used by `ffn_exit`, defers whenever the fused kernel would.
  - **Otherwise it defers** whenever the next layer would run exactly the reduction the FFN would have: one full-precision sum over the same TP group object, on a plain partial sum.
  - **Excluded:**
    - attention DP (handled in the next PR);
    - MoE combines that already sum (a2a, FP4 all-gather, DWDP);
    - quantized communication;
    - a replicated TP1 shared expert;
    - LoRA;
    - EP × MoE-TP hybrids;
    - MoE groups that are not the TP group object.
  - **Applies to `ffn_exit` models.** The models that call `should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer` themselves (Step-3.5, Qwen3.5, MiniMax-M3, GLM5-Next, Dots3, Nemotron-H) still defer only when the fused kernel runs. #41198 moves the first five onto `ffn_exit`.
  - When the fused kernel does not take the batch, or a post-residual addition must be added, `prepare_attn` all-reduces the pending sum and then takes the same quant-format residual step as a complete input. That fallback used to apply a plain norm and drop `quant_format` and `post_residual_addition`.

## Accuracy Tests

No numeric change: the next layer runs the same all-reduce over the same group on the same buffer.

- **`UnreducedOutput`:**
  - **`prepare_attn` call-sequence comparison** (all collectives and kernels stubbed): 24,576 cases identical to the parent.
  - **GPU, H200, 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared; each configuration's audit shows the deferral happening.** Seven configurations are bit-identical: GLM-4.7-Flash TP2, PP2 × TP2 and TP2 + NextN; gpt-oss-120b TP2 + EAGLE3 (aux capture); Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2; Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B TP2 image requests (deepstack); Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2.
- **Deferral without the fused kernel:**
  - **Call sequences:** 22,528 of 24,576 cases are identical. The other 2,048 change in exactly one way: a pending sum is all-reduced first and then takes the normal path.
  - **GPU, H200, 15 configurations bit-identical to the parent:** GLM-4.7-Flash TP2 (fusion on, off, ~3000-token prompt, PP2 × TP2, + NextN); DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 (on / off); Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 (off); gpt-oss-120b TP2 (off, + EAGLE3 on / off); Ling-3.0-flash TP4 (on / off); Laguna-M.1 TP4 (on / off). In the fusion-off configurations the parent never defers and this PR does.

Under `torch.compile`, building the wrapper is a graph break: with `fullgraph=True`, torch 2.13 raises `Unsupported: object.__new__ user-defined class construction`. Decode compiles without `fullgraph`, so a deferring layer splits the compiled graph there. The `tc_piecewise` prefill backend compiles with `fullgraph` and cannot trace a deferring layer; with the second commit that includes prefill at TP > 1 without the fused kernel. The default `breakable` prefill backend is not traced. The `ffn_exit` fullgraph test is removed.

**Two-batch-overlap entry.**

- **CPU test:** a new test hands the entry an `UnreducedOutput` and checks that the split and the merge see the reduced tensor.
- **GPU, B200, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 with two-batch overlap:** the previous revision of this stack crashes at the entry with `AttributeError: 'UnreducedOutput' object has no attribute 'shape'` in four configurations: DeepEP normal mode without attention DP, and attention DP2 with EP2, EP1 and DeepEP.
  - With the fix, each run passes the entry and then stops where main stops in the same configuration. Main stops on a flashinfer MLA ragged-prefill shape check, or on a missing global DP buffer length under two-batch overlap.
  - So there is no bit-identity comparison with two-batch overlap on this machine.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Decode latency, H200, GLM-4.7-Flash TP2 with fusion off, `bench_one_batch` input 512 / output 128, decode CUDA graph on. The two trees ran on separate GPUs, then swapped.

| Batch size | Parent median (ms) | This PR median (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.51 / 6.49 | 6.45 / 6.46 |
| 8 | 8.73 / 8.78 | 8.53 / 8.64 |
| 32 | 12.19 / 11.99 | 12.16 / 11.66 |

The differences are within noise. The all-reduce moves from the end of the FFN to the next layer's `prepare_attn`; the count is the same.
