title: [AMD] Add FlyDSL GDN prefill backend
body:
## Motivation

AITER ships fused FlyDSL implementations of the GDN prepare stages and the K5 state scan for AMD gfx95. Qwen3.5-397B has 45 Gated DeltaNet layers, and at TP4 each rank runs them with 4 key heads, 16 value heads and K=V=128. On those shapes the FlyDSL path runs a prefill batch 1.4-1.74x faster than SGLang's Triton GDN prefill.

This PR exposes that path as an opt-in prefill backend:

```bash
--linear-attn-prefill-backend flydsl
```

Decode and speculative verification stay on Triton. The backend requires gfx95 and is rejected with deterministic inference or multi-item scoring. It also serves batches that track Mamba state for the radix cache, so it stays active with radix cache on (e.g. AgentX). It falls back to Triton for unsupported input/state shapes, mixed batches, and graph-planned paths.

## Modifications

- Register `flydsl` in the linear-attention backend enum and CLI choices.
- Add `FlyDSLGDNKernel`, which runs AITER's FlyDSL prepare, FlyDSL K5 state scan and output stages.
  - Calls the stages directly instead of `chunk_gated_delta_rule_opt_vk`. That function returns `(o, final_state)`, and `snapshot_dtype` only sets the dtype of the temporary snapshot the output stage consumes, so the per-chunk states `h` never leave the wrapper. Radix-cache Mamba tracking reads `h`, which is why the adapter runs the stages itself and keeps it.
  - The L2-norm and output stages are imported from AITER's private `_triton_kernels` modules. They match AITER `4ad99832823dde2315b361cbd3b54b1c5c12acd5`, the gfx950 `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` and the commit in both ROCm images used below.
  - Uses SGLang's native `[N, H, V, K]` state pool with indexed in-place state updates, and reuses the caller-provided output buffer.
  - Remaps DP-attention padding indices to the pool's padding slot, once per batch.
  - `use_exp2=True` is correct here because FlyDSL's fused prepare computes the gate cumsum itself (#39976 uses `use_exp2=False` because it starts from Triton's natural-log prepare). Recurrent state follows `--mamba-ssm-dtype`; per-chunk snapshots are bf16.
- Build AITER's prefill schedule once per eligible forward batch and reuse it across GDN layers.
- Reject FlyDSL for decode/verify, deterministic inference, and non-gfx95 with actionable errors.
- Unit tests for CLI registration, backend validation, dispatch, the AITER call contract, padding indices, per-batch index reuse, and Triton fallback.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP4, real EAGLE MTP, 200 GSM8K questions, five-shot chat template with thinking disabled:

| Configuration | Triton prefill | FlyDSL prefill |
|---|---:|---:|
| Radix cache on (state tracking active) | 0.975 | 0.970 |
| Radix cache off | 0.985 | 0.980 |

One answer apart in both modes, which is within sampling resolution at 200 questions. Both arms move together between modes. The radix-off row predates the switch to calling AITER's stages directly; kernel numerics are unchanged by it.

Kernel-level comparison of `FlyDSLGDNKernel.extend` against `TritonGDNKernel.extend` on MI355X, TP4 (Hq=4, Hv=16) and TP2 (Hq=8, Hv=32) shapes, K=V=128, BF16 Q/K/V, BF16 and FP32 state, mixed-length batches up to 16K tokens and a padding row:

- output max abs diff <= 9.77e-4
- final state <= 7.84e-3
- per-chunk states `h` <= 1.56e-2 (same shape and chunk order as Triton's; about one bf16 step)
- state slots outside the batch unchanged

Unit tests: `test_gdn_prefill_backend_policy.py` 23 passed.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

4x AMD MI355X (gfx950), TP4/EP1, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, AITER attention and MoE, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, page size 16, EAGLE 3 steps / top-k 1 / 4 draft tokens. Fixed-length runs use `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260913` with radix cache disabled and BF16 SSM; AgentX uses `-20260915` with the recipe's defaults.

Each end-to-end table reports a noise floor, and a delta is called significant only when it exceeds it.

### GDN prefill microbenchmark

One prefill batch through all 45 GDN layers, TP4 per-rank shapes, wall time including the per-batch schedule build:

| Extend tokens | Triton | FlyDSL | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1x1024 | 9.37 ms | 6.67 ms | -28.8% |
| 1x4096 | 10.55 ms | 6.72 ms | -36.3% |
| 4096+4096+2000+512 | 14.89 ms | 10.20 ms | -31.5% |
| 1x8192 | 19.11 ms | 10.98 ms | -42.6% |
| 1x16384 | 37.00 ms | 25.53 ms | -31.0% |

Below ~4K tokens both backends are launch-bound, so the saving there is ~3-4 ms per batch. At the default `--chunked-prefill-size 16384`, a 70K prompt is five chunks of the 16384-token row and saves about 57 ms of GDN prefill.

### InferenceX fixed-sequence-length serving, TP4, low concurrency

InferenceX serving client, fixed 70000-token input / 300-token output, radix cache disabled so every token is prefilled. Floor is the baseline's own run-to-run spread. C1 ran on the merged head; C4 and C8 on `2b0f3e2992`, the same backend before merging main.

Concurrency 1, 60 requests per arm, n=3:

| Metric | Triton | FlyDSL | Delta | Floor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P90 E2E | 3028 ms | 2942 ms | -2.84% | 0.30% |
| P50 E2E | 2938 ms | 2866 ms | -2.46% | 0.93% |
| P90 TTFT | 1766 ms | 1703 ms | -3.55% | 1.32% |
| P50 TTFT | 1751 ms | 1688 ms | -3.60% | 0.90% |
| Total throughput | 23928 tok/s | 24617 tok/s | +2.88% | 0.54% |

Every FlyDSL run beats every Triton run. The 63 ms measured TTFT saving matches the 57 ms predicted from the table above.

Concurrency 4, 240 requests per arm, n=3:

| Metric | Triton | FlyDSL | Delta | Floor | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P50 E2E | 8246 ms | 7959 ms | -3.48% | 1.4% | significant |
| P50 TTFT | 3663 ms | 3532 ms | -3.56% | 1.1% | significant |
| P90 TTFT | 4345 ms | 4245 ms | -2.31% | 9.9% | within noise |
| P90 E2E | 9171 ms | 9492 ms | +3.50% | 11.8% | within noise |
| Total throughput | 33986 tok/s | 35222 tok/s | +3.64% | 1.3% | significant |

Concurrency 8, 240 requests per arm, n=3:

| Metric | Triton | FlyDSL | Delta | Floor | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P50 E2E | 14591 ms | 14141 ms | -3.09% | 0.8% | significant |
| P50 TTFT | 3436 ms | 3280 ms | -4.56% | 1.5% | significant |
| P90 TTFT | 4832 ms | 4619 ms | -4.41% | 5.4% | within noise |
| P90 E2E | 16936 ms | 17095 ms | +0.94% | 5.2% | within noise |
| Total throughput | 38403 tok/s | 39665 tok/s | +3.29% | 0.8% | significant |

At C4 and C8 the P90 tail is set by prefill queueing, so its floor stays at 5-12% however many requests we run; only C1 resolves P90. At 8K/1K prefill is ~4% of a request and the backend can reach at most ~0.14% of E2E, well under that shape's 8.1% floor.

### AgentX, TP4 concurrency 4

Private reproduction of the AgentX recipe (`qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh`, `--random-seed 42`), 3600 s per point on an exclusive node. Both arms are `67fc5b96` and differ only by `--linear-attn-prefill-backend`. The PR head adds the once-per-batch index remap on top of that commit; kernel timings match, so this result still applies. Points ran ABBA to cancel a run-order effect. Each value is the mean of an arm's two runs; the floor is the larger of the two arms' run-to-run spreads.

| Metric | Triton | FlyDSL | Delta | Floor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P90 E2E (s) | 10.220 | 10.025 | -1.90% | 4.4% |
| P50 E2E (s) | 1.997 | 1.958 | -1.94% | 4.1% |
| P90 TTFT (s) | 1.017 | 1.016 | -0.04% | 5.1% |
| P50 TTFT (s) | 0.539 | 0.550 | +2.12% | 4.0% |
| Interactivity (tok/s/user) | 251.3 | 250.1 | -0.46% | 2.4% |
| Total throughput (tok/s) | 23387 | 23711 | +1.39% | 4.8% |

Completed requests over the two runs were 1920 (Triton) and 1944 (FlyDSL). Everything is within noise: no regression, and no gain claimed. Throughput and request counts depend on which trajectories each hour-long run reaches, so the latency rows are the ones to read. The recipe hits a ~93% prefix-cache rate, so a typical prefill batch has only a few thousand new tokens. At that size the backend saves ~3-4 ms per batch, under 1% of TTFT and below this benchmark's floor.

This uses Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4; upstream AgentX now uses the AttnFP8-V2 variant. GDN dimensions are identical, so the kernel result carries over.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not needed: a new value for an existing flag.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [HiCache] Preserve all MTP KV and recurrent state
body:
## Motivation

An Inkling MTP request that reuses a HiCache prefix must recover every draft head's KV and convolution/recurrent state. The hybrid SWA/Mamba path omitted separate draft state, and its transfer schedule could leave later draft heads unrestored. Inkling also addresses draft SWA buffers with full-token IDs, while target SWA uses independently allocated physical IDs; packing both into the target SWA host pool copies the wrong draft rows.

This change supports all-SWA, mixed, and all-full MTP draft attention. A host hit restores every draft's state before the final target-layer completion event, using the indices owned by each pool.

## Modifications

- Expose Inkling's checkpoint MTP depth to packed-cache discovery and collect every separate draft convolution/temporal pool. Validate compatible state-slot ownership and avoid packing shared target state twice.
- Preserve Inkling's global MTP depth IDs during single-block runner setup, so SWA heads at depth 2 and later receive SWA pools.
- Pack full-attention draft KV into the full host pool. Pack SWA drafts that share target SWA indices into the SWA host pool. Give identity-mapped SWA drafts a separate host pool derived from full-token indices, preserving their SWA head geometry and including their memory in fixed HiCache budgets.
- Pack compatible draft convolution/temporal state, and schedule all packed KV/state restores within the target transfer range. Keep the portable per-layer NPU fallback for separate state allocations.
- Add registered CPU/GPU regressions for config setup, pool discovery, byte-exact restoration, distinct target/draft indices, mixed attention, and host-memory accounting.

No new flags. The existing MXFP8 host-cache restriction on packed MTP remains.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on base `248c202b46d4a44ad46a3f09d48661b0d9ce6257`:

- **105 tests and 16 subtests passed**, including assembly, HiCache dispatch, layer setup, and packed-state regressions.
- **64 GPU transfer cases** on NVIDIA GB300: all-SWA/mixed/all-full drafts and legacy shared-SWA indexing, BF16/FP16 KV, kernel/direct transfers, differing full/SWA head counts, two/four target layers versus three drafts, convolution-only/convolution-plus-temporal state, and ratio/fixed host sizing. Tests clear device buffers after backup and compare every restored byte at different destination slots.
- **Four end-to-end serving cases** with generated Inkling checkpoints: `sss`, `sfs`, and `fff` draft patterns with kernel I/O, plus `sfs` with direct I/O. All restored **768 host tokens and 0 device-cache tokens** after device eviction. Each generated **32 identical tokens with zero logprob difference** versus a cold run and reported 31 speculative verification steps.
- All applicable upstream pre-commit checks passed for the full PR diff, including CI registration against the PR base.

Serving used BF16, FA4, torch GEMM, TP1, write-through HiCache, and disabled CUDA graphs. The environment had sgl-kernel 0.4.6.post1+cu130, so serving bypassed the tree's 0.4.7 minimum-version check. These are synthetic-weight correctness tests, not trained-model accuracy or acceptance-rate measurements. GPU unit tests bypass controller background threads; serving exercises the actual scheduler/controller. NPU state copying was checked with CPU tensors, not NPU hardware. External L3 storage was not exercised.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark or performance claim. Host allocations account for packed drafts and the SWA sidecar, including fixed-budget coverage.

## Checklist

- [x] Run formatting and pre-commit checks on changed files.
- [x] Add and run registered CPU and GPU regression tests.
- [x] Run Inkling MTP + HiCache serving through device eviction and host restoration.
- [x] Explain behavior and validation limits.

Developed with AI assistance.

title: [mem_cache] Drop `is_insert` from `cache_finished_req`; release rows from `release_kv_cache`
body:
## Summary
- Drop `is_insert` from `cache_finished_req`: the tree only ever inserts; a request that leaves without inserting (abort, retract, transfer failure, sampling-mask finish) is released by `release_kv_cache(is_insert=False)` itself, with `free_kv_row` + `unpin` and no tree call
- Add `BasePrefixCache.unpin(req)` (request-level `dec_lock_ref`; unified releases with its lock receipt), `claim_kv_row(req)` (a streaming session takes the row and the caller releases nothing) and `on_release(req, *, inserted)` (per-request cleanup a cache keeps outside the tree)
- `release_kv_cache` is one linear function: early-mamba / session takeover, optional insert, free `[cache_protected_len, owned_kv_len)`, over-allocated tail, `unpin`, `on_release`, return the row

## Changes
**Tree backends**
- `RadixCache`: share the insert step of `cache_unfinished_req` / `cache_finished_req` in one private `_adopt`; the finished path is adopt, `free_kv_row` the rest, `unpin`
- `PureSWARadixCache`: build on `_adopt` with a key cut at the aligned `swa_evict_floor`; its inserts now carry `req.priority` like `RadixCache` (was 0)
- `UnifiedRadixCache`: pp-prefetch ticket release and streaming-session takeover move to `claim_kv_row`; component cleanup for the no-insert case moves to `on_release`; the disabled branch frees from `cache_protected_len` instead of 0
- `LMCRadixCache` / `FlexKVRadixCache`: load-back marker and session cleanup for the no-insert case move to `on_release`
- `StreamingSession`: `claim_kv_row` wraps `try_cache_finished_req`; `cache_finished_req` is a plain pass-through

**Cleanup**
- Read `req.skip_radix_cache_insert` and `req.priority` directly instead of `getattr`
- Trim the docstrings on the touched methods

## Behavior
- No behavior change on the release paths except the two noted above (pure-SWA node priority, unified disabled branch); verified by replaying scheduler-facing `release_kv_cache` scenarios through radix / pure-SWA / unified against the base commit and diffing allocator, pool and tree state (67/69 identical, the 2 diffs are the intended priority change)

title: [Session] Fix admission and wait for all DP open acknowledgments
body:
## Motivation

Opening a native session can return after only global TP0 has installed it. An immediate generation routed to another attention-DP queue can reach that queue before its session exists. Missing/closing sessions and requests rejected by `Session.create_req` can then enter model or PD admission instead of returning their original error.

## Modifications

- Acknowledge installation from every attention-DP queue leader and await those responses with a per-session `FanOutCommunicator`. Different session opens remain concurrent; cancellation removes the response waiter.
- Recognize pending and completed session aborts and emit the existing terminal response before queue admission, preserving the original error and an active streaming request's ownership.
- Add 17 deterministic CPU cases covering rejection in aggregate/prefill/decode modes, delayed DP leaders under both control-broadcast modes, concurrent opens, failed acknowledgments, cancellation, and TP/CP/PP response ownership.

This targets `main` independently; deferred session cleanup is covered separately in #41190. Related work: #40252 also changes direct session rejection as part of a broader streaming-checkpoint fix; this PR additionally fixes the DP open acknowledgment race and missing/closing-session admission.

## Accuracy Tests

- **90 CPU tests passed:** 17 new cases and 73 existing fan-out, multimodal cleanup, PD queue cleanup, chunked-abort, session-cache, weight-version, and scheduler-timeout cases.
- Against unchanged upstream `2f2f9d12f8485629e162c8fba0e44057fa5d8f97`, the rejection/leader-acknowledgment subset has **7 failing regressions and 3 passing controls**. The same cases pass with this patch.
- Upstream pre-commit checks passed on all four changed files, including test registration and pytest entry-point checks.

Focused test command in a configured SGLang CPU development environment:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_session_admission.py
```

Local validation used Python 3.13, Torch 2.11 CPU, and SGLang's macOS platform import stubs. The tests use real scheduler/session/tokenizer methods with transport and cache boundary fakes; synchronization uses explicit queues and event-loop turns, without timing thresholds.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No GPU, HTTP-server, distributed integration, or throughput run. The DP membership count is captured per open; elastic membership changes during an open are outside the tested scope.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit on changed files.
- [x] Add behavioral unit tests registered in the CPU suite.
- [x] Consider documentation; no public API or configuration additions.
- [ ] GPU accuracy and speed benchmarks (not run).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Session] Defer cleanup until in-flight requests finish
body:
## Motivation

Closing or expiring an ordinary native session during generation can release image inputs and cache state still owned by an unfinished request. A chunked abort can also become terminal before its outstanding forward result stops using those inputs.

## Modifications

- Extend the existing `close_on_finish`/`maybe_reap` workflow to wait for every retained ordinary-session request to finish and for outstanding middle chunks to drain. Preserve the streaming in-flight guard.
- Let `SessionController` own deferred radix-cache release; radix-only sessions retain direct release.
- Mark ordinary-session requests terminal when sending queue-abort notifications that bypass batch-result processing, allowing deferred cleanup to complete after cancellation or queue-full rejection.
- Add eight CPU cases covering close/expiry with shared image ownership, requested versus confirmed abort, queued cancellation/rejection, delayed chunk results, streaming first turns, and radix-only close. Update two existing non-session request fixtures.

This targets `main` independently; admission and DP open acknowledgments are covered separately in #41189. Related work: #40250 addresses streaming/rank-coordinated reaping, and #40251 addresses broader queue-abort cleanup. This PR focuses on the existing close/reap workflow for retained ordinary-session owners and delayed chunks. Requests detached from `Session.req_nodes` by native replacement/pruning remain outside this ownership guarantee.

## Accuracy Tests

- **81 CPU tests passed:** eight new cases and 73 existing fan-out, multimodal cleanup, PD queue cleanup, chunked-abort, session-cache, weight-version, and scheduler-timeout cases.
- Against unchanged upstream `2f2f9d12f8485629e162c8fba0e44057fa5d8f97`, the new suite has **7 failing regressions and 1 passing radix-only control**. All eight pass with this patch.
- Upstream pre-commit checks passed on all five changed files, including test registration and pytest entry-point checks.

Focused test command in a configured SGLang CPU development environment:

title: feat(npu): Support returning indexer top-k results
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

`enable_return_indexer_topk` currently supports the CUDA indexer path, but the NPU backend does not create an indexer-topk capturer or expose the top-k results produced by NPU attention indexers.

  Ascend NPU already provides indexer implementations for:

  - DeepSeek DSA models, through `torch_npu.npu_lightning_indexer`
  - DeepSeek-V4 C4 indexers, through `torch.ops.custom.npu_quant_lightning_indexer`

  However, their results were not connected to the existing request-level return pipeline. As a result, NPU inference requests could not return indexer top-k metadata even when `--enable-return-indexer-topk` and `return_indexer_topk=true` were specified.

  This PR connects the NPU producer paths to the existing indexer-topk capturer and response pipeline while preserving the same output format and layer-index semantics as the CUDA implementation.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Enable indexer-topk capturer creation on both CUDA and NPU backends.
    - Model-specific layer counts continue to be resolved through `get_num_indexer_layers()`.
    - DSA models use one capturer slot per transformer layer.
    - DeepSeek-V4 uses one capturer slot per C4 compression layer.

- Add indexer-topk capture to the NPU DSA path.
    - Capture results from `forward_dsa_prepare_npu()`.
    - Cover both freshly computed top-k results and `skip_topk` layers that reuse the previous layer's result.
    - Preserve the transformer layer id in the capturer layout.

- Add indexer-topk capture to the NPU DeepSeek-V4 C4 path.
    - Capture the output of `npu_quant_lightning_indexer`.
    - Use `token_to_kv_pool.layer_mapping[].compress_layer_id` to map raw transformer layers to contiguous C4 capturer slots.
    - Keep the captured indices in the logical compressed-token coordinate system used by the NPU sparse attention path.

- Extend overlap result handling to NPU.
    - Reuse the existing `TopkCaptureOutput` and result-finalization pipeline.
    - Add NPU support to asynchronous device-to-host copies through `torch.get_device_module()`.
    - Preserve the existing synchronous path when overlap scheduling is disabled.

- Add unit tests covering:
    - NPU DSA capturer initialization.
    - DeepSeek-V4 C4 layer-count resolution.
    - Non-indexer models being disabled through a zero indexer-layer count.
    - Invalid `index_topk` configurations.

title: [DSV4] Account for FlashMLA physical KV page padding in memory budgets
body:
## Motivation

DSV4's FlashMLA KV budget charges every latent slot at 584 bytes, but allocation rounds each physical page to the layout's alignment. With a 256-token logical page, V4 SWA/C4 slots cost 585 bytes each and C128 slots cost 864 bytes each. The resulting underestimate grows with token capacity.

## Modifications

Use the pool's layout selection and `KVLayout.page_bytes()` to price SWA, C4, and C128 at their respective physical page sizes. Keep the existing row costs for unified KV, TRTLLM, HIP, and NPU. This corrects the per-token coefficient; fixed reserved-page accounting is unchanged.

Add one 25-line regression for SWA, C4, and C128 page costs, reusing the existing test fixture.

## Accuracy Tests

- Configurator, compressed-pool, and unified-FP8 CPU suites passed in [GitHub CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36021297860) at `da467a5eeb`, including the compact regression.
- Actual CPU buffer allocations were checked against the budget during development; the regression uses those verified byte costs.
- Pre-commit checks passed.
- DSV4 FlashMLA e2e sanity passed on a 4xB200 devbox (2026-09-25): `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, TP4, `--dsv4-attn-backend flashmla --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`; server reached ready and `/v1/completions` returned 200. Startup log confirmed `dsv4_attn_backend=flashmla` and `bytes_per_full_token=7758.75` (padded FlashMLA page-cost path).

No full model accuracy benchmark rerun: this changes capacity budgeting only, without changing kernels or KV representation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No serving throughput benchmark was run. The byte costs above were checked against actual CPU buffer allocations.

title: [NPU] Support dsv4 dspark on ascend 950
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Enable DeepSeek V4 DSpark speculative decoding on NPU Ascend 950 (arch35). The existing DSpark implementation only supported CUDA and older NPU (arch22). Arch35 hardware requires different sparse-attention operators, weight-loading strategies, and numerical compatibility workarounds. Several follow-up fixes address a regression where DSpark's unquantized `wo_a` path conflicted with the arch35 MXFP8 detection logic, plus NPU-specific numerical gaps.

## Modifications

- **arch35 DSpark sparse attention**: Added arch35-specific v2 sparse attention operators via a new `TorchOpLoader` extension; loaded during TP worker and DSpark draft worker initialization.
- **`wo_a` quantization fix**: `use_npu_arch35_mxfp8_wo_a()` now accepts a `wo_a_keeps_quant_config` parameter and returns `False` when DSpark explicitly disables `wo_a` quantization. This fixes a regression introduced by a previous commit that changed the assertion condition from `if fp8:` to `if quantize_wo_a:`, which caused an incorrect assertion on arch35 because DSpark's `wo_a` was not quantized. The model also caches this value instead of recomputing it at each call site.
- **DSpark stage configuration**: Added `_dspark_stage_config()` to apply draft-specific expert counts to draft stages and disable vision layers for text-only stages. Arch35 now falls back to standard vocabulary/fusion behavior instead of the arch31-specific path.
- **Weight loading**: Moved the NPU `weight_packed` → `weight` rename before stacked parameter mapping, eliminating duplicated branch logic.
- **NPU numerical compatibility**: Fall back to torch for commit-KV projection on NPU; replaced `exponential_()` (unsupported on NPU) with `uniform_ + log_ + neg_`.

title: [Fix] Allocate SWA KV pools inside the memory-saver region
body:
## Summary
`release_memory_occupation` now frees the KV cache of MHA, MLA and DSA sliding-window models.

## Symptom & Reproduction
- **Symptom:** with `--enable-memory-saver`, releasing `kv_cache` leaves the KV cache of SWA models resident, and every DSA model keeps its index-K buffers.
- **Engine measurement:** an H200 TP2 engine of a hybrid SWA model used 85.3 GiB after load, 32.9 GiB after releasing everything, and 85.3 GiB after resuming only the weights, so only the weights were pausable.
- **Reproduction:** build a pool through its `KVCacheConfigurator` builder with the flag on, pause the torch_memory_saver `kv_cache` tag, and read `torch.cuda.mem_get_info`; expected: the pool's bytes are freed; observed on the merge base: 0 GiB freed for all three SWA pool kinds.

## Root Cause
1. `pause(GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE)` unmaps only buffers allocated inside a memory-saver region.
2. `_build_hybrid_swa_kv_pool` never passes the flag, so `SWAKVPool` gives both sub-pools `False`.
3. `_build_hybrid_mla_swa_kv_pool` hard-codes `False` in the explicit sub-pool kwargs it hands `SWAKVPool`.
4. `IndexKeyCache.__init__` allocates index-K outside `memory_saver_adapter.region`, in every DSA pool.

## Fix
Each pool builder now passes `get_exec().features.enable_memory_saver`, as every other pool builder already does. The MHA builder uses a new `SWAKVPool` argument that is forwarded to both sub-pools and defaults to `False`. The hybrid MLA/DSA builder sets the flag in its explicit `common` kwargs, because explicit sub-pool kwargs bypass that argument. `IndexKeyCache` allocates index-K inside the `GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE` region, like the MLA buffers of the same pool. With the flag off the adapter is a no-op, so allocation is unchanged. Unchanged: the NPU SWA path, `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache.remote_buffer` and the DSA compress-tail buffers.

## Verification
- `pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files at this head: passed.
- Pause/resume on one H200 with torch_memory_saver 0.0.9.post1: pools built through the real builders (48 layers, 12 full and 36 SWA), freed GiB per tree:

| tree | MHA SWA (21.0) | hybrid MLA (5.9) | hybrid DSA (6.3, index-K 0.39) |
|---|---|---|---|
| merge base `6fe4b66f5c` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `f9b27e254a` | 21.2 | 0 | 0 |
| builder change only | 21.2 | 6.0 | 6.0 |
| this head `29bc585196` | 21.2 | 6.0 | 6.4 |

- After resume every paused buffer kept its `data_ptr`, read back zero, and accepted writes.
- Not run: a full engine with a hybrid MLA/DSA model, or the NPU path.

## Review Focus
- `index_key_cache.py`: index-K now joins the `kv_cache` tag for every DSA model; resume zero-fills it, and `flush_cache()` runs right after the pause, so stale index-K is never read.
- `_build_hybrid_mla_swa_kv_pool`: its explicit sub-pool kwargs bypass the `SWAKVPool` argument, so the flag must stay in `common`.

title: [Unified Cache] Abort requests whose external linker load fails instead of crashing the scheduler
body:
## Motivation

With the external cache linker (Mooncake / UMBP direct L3), any storage read error during a layer-wise load raised inside the model forward and brought the whole server down (SIGQUIT). Nodes were also published to the radix tree before their KV landed, so simply catching the error would have let other requests reuse unloaded slots.

## Modifications

- A linker load now lands in device slots private to the loading request. `load_back` no longer inserts the tail; the request inserts it like computed KV once the load is confirmed (`load_back_is_cache_owned()` keeps `cache_protected_len` at the device hit).
- `LayerWiseLoadCounter.wait_until` no longer raises. After the forward, `run_batch` calls `finish_external_linker_loads()`, which waits for the batch's load and agrees on the result across ranks (MIN), since an MLA dedup peer never sees the source's error.
- Requests whose load failed are aborted with 503 and never inserted into the tree; chunked requests go through the existing chunked-abort path. The MLA dedup source still issues its layer broadcasts on failure, so peers do not hang.
- The two backends share one `LayerWiseLoadCounter` (first commit, behavior-neutral). The pending-load locks, the load completion queues, and the COMMIT / adopted-page load phase are removed.
- A failed forward commits no output (token or embedding) and is aborted like a sampling-mask failure; PD prefill aborts it instead of sending its KV to decode. A refused `load()` frees its slots and falls back to recompute.
- An SWA branch point placed before the L3 hit was known is dropped once the loaded tail covers it.

## Tests

- `test_unified_cache_linker.py`: request-private load, dedup on insert, failed-load cleanup (Full and Full+SWA) on both tree cores, cross-rank verdict, counter semantics.
- End to end with Mooncake on DeepSeek-V3.2 (TP1, and TP2 with `--enable-linker-mla-dedup`), injecting a mid-load failure: the request gets a 503, the server keeps serving, and the next identical request hits L3 with output identical to a cold run.

## Accuracy and performance

Base = upstream `86cb4a0f97`, PR = this branch. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 on 4x H200, the cookbook H200 FP8 low-latency recipe (TP4 + EAGLE 3/1/4) plus `--enable-unified-cache-external-linker` with Mooncake. Every phase starts from a flushed device cache; two runs per side (base/PR, then PR/base).

**Performance** — `bench_serving`, random 4096 in / 256 out, 128 prompts, concurrency 16. Mean of two runs.

| Scenario | Side | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Backup only (no hit, 0/128 L3 loads) | base | 479.7 | 348.5 | 13.8 | 1016 |
| | PR | 459.5 | 351.6 | 13.9 | 1014 |
| Backup + load-back (same prompts, 128/128 L3 loads, 94% prefill hit) | base | 354.7 | 348.7 | 13.4 | 1070 |
| | PR | 335.0 | 358.2 | 13.0 | 1108 |

All deltas are inside the run-to-run spread (e.g. base load-back mean TTFT was 395 / 314 ms across its two runs).

**Accuracy** — run twice on one server: cold, then again after a device flush so prompts come back from L3.

| Eval | Side | Cold | After flush (L3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 q (74 L3 loads after flush) | base | 0.954 / 0.955 | 0.953 / 0.951 |
| | PR | 0.955 / 0.952 | 0.955 / 0.957 |
| mixed-prefix gsm8k, 1000 q (~810 L3 loads after flush) | base | 0.966 | 0.967 |
| | PR | 0.969 | 0.968 |

Prefill hit tokens and L3 load counts match between base and PR in every phase.

title: [sglang-miles] Colocated RL for hybrid-state models: flush order, bf16 MoE weight-update layout, R3 routed-experts capture
body:
Three fixes needed for colocated RL on hybrid-state models (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, GLM-5.3-Flash) on current `sglang-miles`. Supersedes #40815, which is folded in here as the first commit.

## Motivation

1. **Hybrid state pools fault with CUDA error 700 at memory release.** `release_memory_occupation` paused (unmapped) the KV cache memory-saver region and only then called `flush_cache()`. The hybrid pools cleared there (mamba states, qwen4_exp PLE `ShortConvPool` / `NgramPool`, KDA state) live inside that region and their `clear()` writes device memory, so the write hits unmapped memory. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the fault lands on `ShortConvPool.clear()` via `release_memory_occupation -> flush_cache -> HybridReqToTokenPool.clear`. The trainer's later `/flush_cache` while the engine is offloaded faults the same way.
2. **bf16 MoE weight update crashes on plain `flashinfer_trtllm`.** The TRT-LLM bf16 postprocess repacks `w13`/`w2` into block layout for every TRT-LLM MoE runner variant, but `maybe_restore_flashinfer_trtllm_bf16_weight_shape_for_load` only restored the canonical shape for `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`. On GB300 the auto backend resolves to plain `flashinfer_trtllm`, so the first weight sync failed with `size of tensor a (64) must match tensor b (4096) at dimension 2`.
3. **R3 routed-experts capture silently returns zeros.** On SM100, `moe_runner_backend=auto` resolves to `flashinfer_trtllm` for Glm5Next, which fuses routing into the kernel, so `capture_routed_experts_if_allowed` never runs and `--enable-return-routed-experts` ships the zero-initialized buffer. The trainer then replays expert-0 rows and alltoall dies with `Split sizes doesn't match total dim 0 size`.

## Modifications

1. `weight_updater.py`: flush before tagging the KV region as offloaded and pausing it (the tag is what makes the later flush a no-op). `Scheduler.flush_cache`: return success without clearing while the KV region is released (the pools were flushed right before the pause).
2. `unquant.py`: gate the shape restore on `self.use_flashinfer_trtllm_moe`, the same flag that gates the repack.
3. `overrides.py` + `moe_hook.py`: a `_routed_experts_capture_backend_guard` pass, run after every `moe_runner_backend` resolution. With `enable_return_routed_experts`, a topk-bypassing runner (`flashinfer_trtllm`, `experimental_sgl_trtllm`, `triton_kernel`, `flashinfer_mxfp4`) is rejected with an error that names a topk-materializing runner to pass instead (miles' GLM-5.3-Flash launcher passes `--sglang-moe-runner-backend triton`).

## Validation

Full-model colocated RL e2e, 8 nodes x 4 GB300, latest `radixark/miles:dev`, `--colocate`, R3 routing replay, CUDA graph on:

- radixark/miles#2777 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): without fix 1, all four engines die with CUDA error 700 at the first memory release. With it: 5 rollouts / 5 train steps, weight-update equality check passes, `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` 0.0083 to 0.0131, raw reward 0.47 to 0.75.
- radixark/miles#2786 (GLM-5.3-Flash bf16): 4 rollouts / 3 train steps, `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` 0.0085 / 0.0098 / 0.0087, raw reward 0.50 to 0.72; routed experts were captured with the triton runner.

title: Fix Responses API additional_tools input handling
body:
## Motivation

`/v1/responses` rejects `additional_tools` before inference:

```text
Unsupported Responses API input item type: 'additional_tools' None
```

This breaks Codex auto-review. It also reproduces with a direct request, so it is not specific to Codex. `additional_tools` is [documented Responses API input](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search#add-tools-at-a-specific-point-in-the-input).

This request should make `get_weather` available to the model:

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
  "input": [
    {
      "type": "additional_tools",
      "role": "developer",
      "tools": [{
        "type": "function",
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather for a city.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["city"]
        }
      }]
    },
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Paris? Use the tool."}
  ]
}
```

## Modifications

- Keep the tool definitions where they were added in the conversation.
- Include them in tool-choice validation and output parsing, including streaming.
- Preserve them through `previous_response_id` and reject duplicate tool names.

Kimi and DeepSeek use message-level tool schemas. Other chat templates get the schemas as developer-labelled text. Harmony uses a developer tool message.

Supports function and custom tools on the chat path, and function tools on Harmony. Namespace and built-in tools in `additional_tools` return 400.

## Tests

437 CPU tests passed:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai \
  test/registered/unit/function_call/test_deepseekv41_detector.py
```

The repro fails on unpatched main at `a1eb691ab5`. The patched test uses the real DeepSeek V4.1 encoder and DSML parser and returns `get_weather({"city":"Paris"})`, including streaming and a stored continuation. Tokenization and inference are mocked. This is not a live model test.

Also covers declaration order, mixed top-level and inline tools, custom calls, `tool_choice="none"`, invalid definitions and Harmony replay.

Pre-commit checks passed.

title: [ROCm] topk v2: split one long row across blocks, the CDNA cluster-path equivalent
body: **Where this helps:** ROCm decode top-k with a small batch over a long context — the shape a reasoning model spends its time in. It engages at `batch_size <= 64` once rows pass a batch-dependent floor (40K at small batch), and is worth most at batch 1-8 over 128K or more: 1.8-3.0x on the kernel, geomean 1.56x across everything the gate admits. Everything else is gated off and unchanged. On GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4 on MI355X: **1.41x on the decode top-k kernel** and **-3.8% median ITL** at 120K context, batch 1. ## The problem Decode top-k is parallelism-bound, not bandwidth-bound. One block owns one row, so a batch of 8 over a 128K window puts 8 blocks on a 256-CU GPU and scans 512 KB twice in each. CUDA splits a row across a thread-block cluster; CDNA has neither clusters nor DSMEM, so on ROCm that shape just runs narrow. Before After ## What this does Two launches cooperating through global memory, with the kernel boundary as the barrier. Nothing spins. 1. `topk_split_hist` — each rank histograms its chunk into the row's histogram (counted in LDS, one global atomic per non-empty bin). 2. `topk_split_select` — each rank re-reads it, derives the threshold, rescans and appends its candidates. The last rank to arrive resolves the tie tail, re-zeroes the histogram, and applies the page-table transform. | | | |---|---| | `split` | `clamp(64 / batch_size, 4, 32)` | | fires when | `batch_size <= 64` and `max_seq_len` above the floor | | floor | 40960 / 49152 / 65536 / 114688, by batch | | scratch | ~2 MB, `hipMalloc`'d once per device, never freed (captured HIP graphs hold the address) | Both constants follow from one cost balance. Splitting shortens the scan as `L / split` but pays cross-block cost — atomics in, slots out, an epilogue per row — that grows as `rows * split`. Past ~64 blocks per launch the second term wins badly: 64 rows of 128K cost 115 us spread 32 ways against 34 us spread 4. So cap blocks at 64 rather than chasing the CU count, and key the floor on batch rather than on `split`, since the unsplit path costs the same wall time at any batch that fits the machine while the split path runs its epilogue once per row. ## Scope CUDA is untouched: preprocessing `topk_v2.cuh` without `USE_ROCM` gives a translation unit byte-identical to the baseline's, for `SUPPORT_CLUSTER` 0 and 1. Prefill / ragged / packed cannot reach the new path — separate entry points, and `batch_size <= 64` excludes any prefill chunk. One file plus its test. ## Correctness `test_topk_v2.py` on gfx950: **294 passed** (288 existing + 6 new), `negative_infinity` 5 passed. The invariant is that the selected set matches `torch.topk` exactly, ties included. The existing suite reaches the gate but cannot check that — its tie tests use rows of a few hundred elements, and its long rows are `randn`, whose threshold bin never fills — so `test_topk_v2_split_duplicate_scores` fills it, with rows of `nvals` distinct scores putting `seq / nvals` exact duplicates at the cut. That also sets the histogram width. The threshold bin is resolved from at most `kMaxNumTie` staged candidates, so a bin holding more *unequal* scores than that silently drops the rest; this path matches the 12 bits of the `TopKStreaming` it replaces on ROCm rather than the 10 of the CUDA cluster path, and on 128K rows of `randint(0, n)` it is exact for every `n` from 32 to 16384, as is the baseline. 12 bits is free in LDS (the histogram overlays `tie_values`, 16 KB either way) and costs 1 MB of scratch; the time it is not free in is what the 64-block cap pays for. ROCm-only test, since CUDA takes its cluster path here. ## Performance Baseline throughout is `topk_v2` at this PR's parent commit — the kernel this PR edits, and the one GLM takes on ROCm since #36851 turned it on by default. The other ROCm implementation, the native `topk.hip` cooperative kernel from [#37591](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37591), sits behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=0` and is not touched here. MI355X, `k=2048`, `page_size=64`, `row_starts=None` so the call reaches `transform_paged`; device time from the profiler, median of three runs of 100 iterations. `B` is the paged entry's `batch_size`, which for this layout is the batch — except under speculative decoding, where the indexer builds `[B * next_n, max_seq_len]` logits and the gate sees the draft-expanded count. 126 points, floor disabled so the losing half is visible rather than assumed: Speedup falls with B and rises with L: the baseline is one block's two scans of one row (flat in B, ~5.5 us + 2.16 us per 10K), the split path is flat in L and grows with B. The gate is the contour where they meet. With it applied — what ships, flat 1.00x below the floor: All 71 points inside the gate are >= 1.00x: worst 1.06x (B=64, 128K), best 3.03x (B=1, 256K), geomean 1.56x. | B | L | before (us) | after (us) | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 128K | 33.50 | 16.70 | **2.01x** | | 8 | 128K | 33.78 | 18.94 | **1.78x** | | 32 | 128K | 33.95 | 25.29 | 1.34x | | 64 | 128K | 35.94 | 33.89 | 1.06x | | 4 | 256K | 53.71 | 19.07 | **2.82x** | | 8 | 64K | 19.51 | 15.13 | 1.29x | | 128 | 128K | 38.11 | 38.08 | 1.00x (outside gate) | | 32 | 40K | 14.82 | 14.84 | 1.00x (below floor) | One caveat on the gate. It reads `max_seq_len` from the score tensor's width, which eager decode sizes to `seq_lens_cpu.max()` but graph capture sizes to the static KV capacity, so under capture a batch of short rows still enters the split dispatch. Selection stays correct — rank 0 retires those rows to the ordinary one-block kernel inline — but the histogram launch still costs a flat ~1.8 us, and there is no host-side fix under capture, where one captured decision must cover every length the graph may replay at. Crossover in *real* length is ~40K, exactly where the floor sits, so the practical consequence is to size `--context-length` to what is served. ## What this is worth in GLM-5.2 GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (quark, 408 GB), TP4 on MI355X, no-MTP recipe, `--context-length 131072`. Each performance pair ran both arms back to back in one session on one set of GPUs; the accuracy pair did not. Full dump in `RESULTS.md`. ### Kernel level Matched `num_steps=300` windows over ISL 70K at concurrency 8, TP0 trace. | ISL 70K, conc 8 | launches | us/call | us/step | |---|---|---|---| | baseline `topk_main_kernel` | 5103 = 243 steps x 21 | 27.73 | 582 | | split `topk_split_hist` | 5124 = 244 steps x 21 | 4.75 | | | split `topk_split_select` | 5124 = 244 steps x 21 | 14.97 | | | split total | | **19.72** | **414** | **1.41x on the kernel**, 168 us back per decode step. Both arms launch 21 times per step — the checkpoint's 21 `full` indexers, confirmed at runtime — so the split changes the cost of a launch and not the structure, and `topk_main_kernel` is absent from the split trace, so the new path is live. Those 168 us are also the end-to-end ceiling: 1.3% of the 12.67 ms step, because the step is bound by weights and all-reduce rather than KV length. Sparse MLA costs 4685 ms and quickreduce 3248 ms against top-k's 101 ms in the same window. ### End to end Median ITL, not TPOT or throughput: at OSL 300 these runs are prefill-dominated (median TTFT 3.0-6.1 s) and prefill is untouched. | config | baseline ITL (ms) | split ITL (ms) | change | TTFT (ms) b/s | |---|---|---|---|---| | ISL 70K / OSL 300, conc 4 | 11.21 | 11.00 | -1.9% | 3001 / 3310 | | ISL 70K / OSL 300, conc 8 | 12.89 | 12.67 | -1.7% | 5845 / 5863 | | ISL 120K / OSL 300, conc 4 | 11.54 | 11.13 | -3.6% | 5685 / 5695 | | ISL 8K / OSL 1024, conc 8 (below floor) | 12.31 | 12.27 | -0.3% | 348 / 350 | | **ISL 120K / OSL 2000, conc 1** | **10.29** | **9.90** | **-3.8%** | 6097 / 6110 | Nothing is slower, and TTFT matching on four of five pairs to within 0.8% confirms the patch stayed inside decode; the 10% spread at 70K/conc 4 is prefill scheduling variance. The last row is the point. At batch 1 the gate opens to `split = 32` against a 120K row, where the unsplit kernel has almost no rows to spread across CUs, and concurrency 1 removes queueing, so the gain lands identically on median ITL (-3.8%), P99 ITL (-3.4%), e2e latency (26.68 -> 25.89 s) and output throughput (75.02 -> 77.19 tok/s). ISL 8K is the config the design expects to lose — rows under the 40960 floor, admitted anyway on the 131072-wide buffer — and it comes out neutral, so the case for a host-supplied real max length is that the gate decides on the wrong quantity, not that the penalty is measurable. (An earlier pass compared arms across a host reboot and had it regressing 1.3% with throughput down 14%, which looked exactly like that penalty and was an artefact.) ### Accuracy | arm | GSM8k (1200q) | invalid | latency (s) | |---|---|---|---| | baseline | 0.933 | 0.000 | 276.9 | | split | 0.926 | 0.000 | 262.2 | 8 questions on n=1200, inside one standard error (0.0074), and selection is exact by the unit tests. Cross-session pair, so this is a check that nothing broke rather than a measurement of 0.007. ## Checklist - [x] `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py` - [x] gfx950 correctness — 294 passed, plus a new duplicate-score test for the cross-rank tie merge - [x] gfx950 kernel-level numbers - [x] CUDA compile check — preprocessed TU byte-identical to baseline without `USE_ROCM`; no CUDA toolchain on the bench box, so a real `nvcc` run still wants CI - [x] GLM-5.2 A/B — 21 launches/step on both arms, 27.73 us -> 19.72 us (1.41x); -1.7% to -3.8% median ITL across five configs, none slower; GSM8k 0.933 -> 0.926 (8 questions on n=1200, inside one standard error) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #35707599106](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35707599106) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35707598765](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35707598765) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35707599380](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35707599380)

title: Support MLA DCP with HiCache file L3 across matching engines
body:
## Why?

- HiCache L3 currently rejects decode context parallelism (DCP). Each MLA rank holds a token shard, so the existing rank-0-only backup cannot save a complete logical page.
- Implements the first stage of #29736: KV reuse between engines with matching TP/DCP sizes.

## What?

- Give equivalent MLA shards shared storage keys and select one writer per shard. Use the same ownership for backups and file eviction/accounting.
- Translate logical host-page starts into local rows for file reads and writes; keep allocation and completion counts in logical tokens.
- Preserve cross-rank prefix agreement and completion acknowledgments after lookup, read, or backup failures.
- Enable startup and runtime attachment for dense BF16 MLA with file storage, `page_first` layout, `kernel` transfers, `write_through`, and `wait_complete`. Keep other configurations guarded.
- Add CPU/distributed tests, a fresh-engine H200 test, and the feature contract with measured evidence. GQA DCP storage and topology conversion remain outside this stage.

## Verification?

Observed on H200 with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`:

```text
Before: TP=4 / DCP=2 + L3 -> startup rejected

After:  TP=4 / DCP=2
  writer rank 0 -> shard 0 -> reader ranks 0, 2
  writer rank 1 -> shard 1 -> reader ranks 1, 3

  8 logical pages -> 16 files
  fresh engine   -> 1,024 restored tokens on every rank
  generated IDs  -> identical to the cold run
```

- Fresh readers passed at TP/DCP `2/2`, `4/2`, and `4/4`; `4/4` also exercised runtime attachment.
- Removing shard 1 of page 2 reduced reuse to 128 tokens on all four ranks; generated IDs still matched the cold run.
- Two concurrent engines left 16 complete objects; a third fresh engine restored the full prefix.
- Reproduce with four free H200 GPUs: `python -m pytest test/manual/hicache/test_dcp_l3.py -q -s`.

## Test?

- Focused CPU suite, including real four-process Gloo failure tests: **64 passed, 63 subtests**.
- HiCache argument regressions: **9 passed, 20 subtests**.
- Unified-cache storage/prefetch regressions: **89 passed, 137 skipped**.
- Final guard checks, including both BF16 spellings: **3 passed, 21 subtests**.
- H200 restore, missing-shard, runtime-attach, and concurrent-writer cases: **passed**.
- Ruff lint/format, import sorting, registered-test validation, and whitespace checks: **passed**.
- GitHub CI: **pending**. Performance benchmarking: **not run**.
- Exact commands, test limitations, and results: [`spec/evidence/feature-00-dcp-l3.md`](https://github.com/ByronHsu/sglang/blob/dcp-hicache-l3/spec/evidence/feature-00-dcp-l3.md).

title: [Kimi-K3] Experiment: shared gate_up on the side stream instead of the merged front
body:
## Motivation

Experiment for the K3 TP MoE front. Today the shared-expert `gate_up` (1536 cols/rank) is folded into the merged front GEMM `[gate | shared gate_up | latent down] = [T,7168] x [7168,6016]`. The usual pattern is to run the whole shared block (`gate_up -> SiTU -> down -> AR`) as one unit on a side stream, overlapping the routed experts. This PR adds an opt-in switch to do exactly that so the two layouts can be A/B'd, and records the measurement.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_K3_GU_SIDE_MIN_TOKENS` (default `0` = off): for MoE batches with `num_tokens >= N`, the front GEMM reads only the `[gate | latent down]` row slice of the merged weight (`[7168,4480]`), and the shared `gate_up` GEMM is issued on `alt_stream` right before SiTU/shared-down/low-SM AR. The merged weight is unchanged (no extra memory); `gate_up` is emitted in fp32 like the front so SiTU sees identical inputs.
- No change when the variable is unset.

## Benchmark (8x GB300 as 2x4 over MNNVL, TP8, `flashinfer_mxfp4`, DSPARK gamma=7, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=4`, in 2048 / out 512, `one_batch_server`, median of 3)

Verify step time (ms), T = 8*bs. Candidate run with `SGLANG_K3_GU_SIDE_MIN_TOKENS=1` (new path at every T).

| bs | T | merged front (main) | gate_up on side stream | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8 | 13.19 | 13.13 | -0.4% |
| 8 | 64 | 26.45 | 26.00 | -1.7% |
| 16 | 128 | 34.48 | 34.15 | -1.0% |
| 32 | 256 | 43.66 | 43.83 | +0.4% |
| 48 | 384 | 52.79 | 52.76 | 0.0% |

Run-to-run spread within each arm is ~1-2%, so none of this is significant. The expected win at T=384 (front N 6016 -> 4480, ~4 us/layer, ~0.4 ms/step) does not materialize: the routed trtllm MoE already saturates the SMs/HBM at these sizes, so the side-stream `gate_up` time-slices with it rather than hiding under it.

**Conclusion so far:** keeping `gate_up` in the 3-way merged front is at least as fast at spec-verify sizes and keeps the single launch / single PDL chain into route+quant. Opened as a draft to keep the switch and the numbers around; not proposing to flip the default.

## Accuracy Tests

Not run (perf experiment, default off).

title: [Fix] MoE: require TopK layer_id to ensure routed expert captures
body:
## Summary
`TopK` now requires `layer_id`, so no MoE model can omit it and break routed-experts capture.

## Symptom & Reproduction
- **Symptom:** with `--enable-return-routed-experts`, MiMo-V2 fails decode CUDA-graph capture with a shape mismatch, `Target sizes: [8, 1, 4, 8]`; 20 other `TopK` calls on `main` (Nemotron-H, Mixtral, Llama 4, DeepSeek, Kimi, ...) omit `layer_id` the same way.
- **Reproduction:** `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <MiMo-V2 checkpoint> --trust-remote-code --tp 4 --enable-return-routed-experts`; expected: graphs capture; observed: the error above.

## Root Cause
1. `TopK.__init__` defaults `layer_id` to `None`, so omitting it is silent.
2. `capture_routed_experts_if_allowed` forwards `layer_id=None` to the capturer.
3. `self.buffer[:batch, layer_id, :]` (`state_capturer/base.py:50`) inserts an axis for `None`.
4. The copy target becomes `[batch, 1, num_layers, top_k]`, so the copy fails.

## Fix
- `TopK.__init__` takes `layer_id: int` with no default, so a model that omits it fails at construction with `TypeError` instead of at capture time. Past fixes went model by model (#30363, #38718) and did not stop the next model from repeating the mistake.
- All 21 calls now pass the id each model already gives its experts. The Nemotron-H line matches #38718 (author Shi Dong kept).
- The DBRX, DeepSeek, Xverse and AFMoE MoE blocks gain a `layer_id` parameter fed by their decoder layer.
- The Triton fused-MoE test and benchmark pass `layer_id=0`.
- Unchanged: calls that already passed `layer_id`, `HashTopK`, and `select_experts`.

## Verification
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` at this head: passed (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, registered-test checks).
- AST scan of the tree at this head: all 47 `TopK(...)` calls pass `layer_id` (`deepseek_v2.py` through `topk_kwargs`), and each passed name is a parameter or an earlier-assigned attribute of the enclosing `__init__`.
- The MiMo-V2 line on the sglang-miles tree (#40977): MiMo-V2.6-Flash engines with `--enable-return-routed-experts` captured CUDA graphs. The Nemotron-H line (#38718): NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 started with routing replay on 8 H200 GPUs.
- Not run on a GPU at this head.

## Review Focus
- `TopK.__init__`: dropping the default makes out-of-tree models that build `TopK` without `layer_id` fail at init with `TypeError`; that is the intended guard.
- `dbrx.py` / `deepseek.py` / `xverse_moe.py` / `afmoe.py`: the new MoE-block `layer_id` parameter has exactly one caller each.

title: [Diffusion][sglang-miles] Bring sglang-miles-h3 H3 rollout commits onto sglang-miles + LoRA-wrap fixes
body:
## Review guide

**TL;DR:** the `sglang-miles-h3` PR + two LoRA fixes.
- 4 H3 cherry-picks: already reviewed on `sglang-miles-h3`, applied cleanly. Skim.
- 2 LoRA fixes: `447815eb7f` (Qwen-Image, +1) and `9895674013` (MiniMax-H3, +3). Review these.

Brings the four commits that exist only on `sglang-miles-h3` onto the current `sglang-miles`. It also fixes two sglang-miles fast paths that break once LoRA wraps a layer, which blocked miles_diffusion RL.

## Cherry-picks (applied cleanly)
- #35598 MiniMax H3 t2va rollout (mirror of #34365)
- #36754 Rollout API: off-loop serialization, spliced msgpack, timing headers, opt-in uint8 video
- #36994 Rollout API: return only SDE latents. miles_diffusion now needs its `latent_step_indices`; without it Wan22 GRPO fails on plain `sglang-miles`.
- #37350 Reuse disk LoRA mapping and FFN swap on H3 IPC updates

## Fixes on top
- **Qwen-Image** (`447815eb7f`): `_get_added_qkv_projections` only takes #36680's packed split path for a bare `MergedColumnParallelLinear`. On a LoRA wrapper it raised `AttributeError: ... no attribute 'output_partition_sizes'`, and it would also have dropped the LoRA delta.
- **MiniMax-H3** (`9895674013`): `_accepts_mxfp8_input` (#37903) returns False for anything that is not a `LinearBase`, so LoRA wrappers stay off the MXFP8 input path. Before this it raised `AttributeError: 'RowParallelLinearWithLoRA' object has no attribute 'quant_method'`.

Both bugs are also on `main`; a separate PR will port them.

## Validation
miles_diffusion e2e is green on this PR (radixark/miles_diffusion#257, 13/13). Four standards were re-recorded for upstream `sglang-miles` changes, not these commits (#37616 for SD3, #36680 for Qwen-Image, #35796 for H3); attribution is in #257.

title: [Score API] Setwise Scoring Support
body: # Setwise Scoring Support ## Summary Adds **setwise scoring** to the score API: a SequenceClassification deployment can read its classification head **at every occurrence of a caller-chosen extraction token** in each `query + item` sequence, instead of only at the last token. A candidate set is packed into one item with one extraction token per candidate, and the head is pooled at each of those positions in a **single forward pass**, so `scores` comes back as one `[N_i x num_labels]` matrix per item (nested per item). This is a generic multi-position pooling primitive (`token_indices_to_pool`) that setwise scoring is the first consumer of; it is designed to extend to token classification, multi-vector embeddings, etc. The feature works in both execution modes: - **Batched (default):** each item is scored as an independent `query + item` sequence in one batch. - **Fused (`--enable-mis`):** the items are fused into one multi-item sequence (block-diagonal mask, shared query-prefix KV). Both modes return the same nested per-item shape. ## Motivation Rerankers and listwise/setwise rankers score a *set* of candidates jointly. Without this feature a caller must issue one request per candidate (last-token pooling), paying the query-prefix cost N times and losing any cross-candidate context. Setwise scoring packs the whole candidate block into one prompt with one anchor token per candidate and returns all N scores from a single prefill, cutting redundant prefill work and giving the head a single fused view of the set. ## API ### Engine (in-process) ```python result = engine.score( query="", # optional shared prefix items=[prompt_with_anchors], # one item = one candidate set score_extraction_token_id=anchor_id, apply_softmax=False, return_pooled_hidden_states=False, ) # result.scores -> [num_items][N_i x num_labels] (nested per item) # result.pooled_hidden_states (optional) parallels scores: per-item, per-anchor vectors ``` `async_score(...)` takes the same `score_extraction_token_id` argument. ### HTTP (`POST /v1/score`) ```json { "query": "", "items": ["Rank the candidates. ... Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>"], "score_extraction_token": "<|object_ref_start|>", "apply_softmax": false } ``` - Request adds `score_extraction_token: Optional[str]` (resolved to an id in the tokenizer-manager process, which owns the tokenizer). - `ScoringResponse.scores` is now a union: `[num_rows x num_labels]` (pointwise) or nested `[num_items][N_i x num_labels]` (setwise). `pooled_hidden_states` follows the same nesting. ### Semantics & validation - SequenceClassification only, and specifically models whose forward routes the head through `score_and_pool` (per-position pooling) — an explicit allow-list (`is_score_and_pool_model`). Generation (CausalLM), cross-encoder (`CrossEncodingPooler`), reward, and embedding models are rejected **before** inference, and `item_first` is incompatible. - An omitted `query` is normalized by item type (`[]` for pre-tokenized items, `""` for text) so token-ID items with no query take the token-ID path. - Every item must contain at least one extraction token; the shared query prefix must not contain it (both raise a clean `400` before inference). - The fused (`--enable-mis`) path carries the standard MIS delimiter tokens, so its scores differ slightly from the independent batched path — the inherent MIS trade-off, not specific to score extraction. ## Deployment / server start Pooling positions are full-prompt coordinates and all positions must be processed in one prefill, so setwise scoring requires radix cache and chunked prefill to be off. These constraints are validated at request time. Batched setwise: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size -1 ``` Fused multi-item setwise (adds MIS): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-mis \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size -1 ``` (`--enable-mis` already auto-disables CUDA graph / radix cache / chunked prefill.) `--allow-auto-truncate` is rejected, since truncation would leave pooling positions pointing past the truncated length. ## Worked example Serving a real multi-task setwise ranker (`num_labels = 7`): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /shared/public/elr-models/sjsmodels/downloaded_models/sps_l3_multitask_ranker_setwise_history_0_0_4_0_peoplesearch-oc_sps_l3_multitask_ranker_setwise_history/proxima/model_resources \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --dtype float16 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.15 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` Two items (candidate sets), each with three anchors → nested `[num_items][N_i x num_labels]` (2 items × 3 rows × 7 labels): ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/score \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "query": "", "items": [ "Rank the candidates. Candidate 0. Candidate 1. Candidate 2. Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>", "Rank the candidates. Candidate 0. Candidate 1. Candidate 2. Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>" ], "score_extraction_token": "<|object_ref_start|>", "apply_softmax": false }' | python -m json.tool ``` ```json { "scores": [ [ [0.7158203125, -0.326171875, -2.576171875, -5.640625, -5.984375, -1.6240234375, -7.328125], [0.72314453125, -0.333984375, -2.560546875, -5.6015625, -5.8203125, -1.6318359375, -7.25390625], [0.7353515625, -0.35302734375, -2.587890625, -5.6171875, -5.6796875, -1.6337890625, -7.1875] ], [ [0.7158203125, -0.326171875, -2.576171875, -5.640625, -5.984375, -1.6240234375, -7.328125], [0.72314453125, -0.333984375, -2.560546875, -5.6015625, -5.8203125, -1.6318359375, -7.25390625], [0.7353515625, -0.35302734375, -2.587890625, -5.6171875, -5.6796875, -1.6337890625, -7.1875] ] ], "pooled_hidden_states": null, "model": "default", "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 42, "total_tokens": 42, "completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "reasoning_tokens": 0 }, "object": "scoring" } ``` (The two items are identical here, so their matrices match; each item independently yields one `[3 x 7]` matrix — one row per candidate anchor, seven task labels wide.) ## Implementation | Area | File | Change | |---|---|---| | Pooling kernel | `layers/pooler.py` | `pool_at_positions()` (pool AT positions, no `delimiter-1` shift, no discarded row) and a multi-position branch in `score_and_pool()`. | | Request plumbing | `managers/io_struct.py` | `token_indices_to_pool` on `EmbeddingReqInput` / `TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput`, split in `__getitem__`. | | | `managers/schedule_batch.py` | `Req.token_indices_to_pool`. | | | `managers/scheduler.py` | Partition prefill batches by pooling mode in `get_new_batch_prefill` so pooling-readout (setwise) and standard requests never share a forward batch — valid requests are never rejected based on concurrent traffic. | | | `managers/scheduler.py` (io), `managers/tokenizer_manager.py` | Thread the field through request construction. | | Forward batch | `model_executor/forward_batch_info.py` | Build per-request `token_indices_to_pool` CPU tensors in `init_new` (mirrors `multi_item_delimiter_indices`; read-only over the ScheduleBatch). | | | `model_executor/model_runner.py` | Skip the prefill CUDA-graph path when `token_indices_to_pool` is set. | | Score engine | `managers/tokenizer_manager_score_mixin.py` | Extraction-token resolution/scanning, omitted-query normalization, capability-based validation, per-item anchor bucketing for MIS, and nested per-item result grouping (`per_item_matrix`). | | | `configs/model_config.py` | `is_score_and_pool_model()` allow-list of SequenceClassification architectures that pool the head per position. | | Entry points | `entrypoints/engine_score_mixin.py` | `score_extraction_token_id` on `score()` / `async_score()`. | | | `entrypoints/openai/protocol.py`, `entrypoints/openai/serving_score.py` | `score_extraction_token` field, token→id resolution, recursive tensor→list conversion for nested `pooled_hidden_states`. | | Tests / bench | `test/registered/unit/...`, `test/registered/e2e/scoring/test_setwise_scoring.py`, `benchmark/prefill_only/bench_setwise_score.py` | Unit + HF-parity + MIS tests and an Engine benchmark. | 16 files, +2080 / -45. ## Review feedback addressed - **Mixed-traffic reliability (High).** Setwise and pointwise requests share the `/v1/score` endpoint and scheduler queue, so a client cannot guarantee homogeneous batches. Rather than reject setwise requests that happen to be batched with pointwise ones, the scheduler now **partitions prefill batches by pooling mode** (`get_new_batch_prefill`): a batch admits only the pooling mode of its first request, and the other mode runs in the next batch. The earlier traffic-dependent 400 abort is removed, restoring the additive/backward-compatible contract. Guarded by `test_mixed_setwise_and_pointwise_concurrent_batch`. - **Omitted `query` for tokenized input (Medium).** `query` now normalizes to `[]` for pre-tokenized items and `""` for text before path selection, so `engine.score(items=[[...token ids...]])` (and HTTP requests with no `query`) take the token-ID path instead of being rejected by the text builder. Guarded by `test_setwise_tokenized_items_omitted_query_match_hf`. - **Eligibility tied to `score_and_pool` (Low).** Validation now uses an explicit allow-list (`is_score_and_pool_model`) of SequenceClassification architectures that pool the head per position, so reward/embedding models (which pool a single vector and would ignore the readout positions) are rejected up front instead of after a wasted forward. Guarded by `test_validation_rejects_reward_model` / `test_validation_rejects_embedding_model`. ## Validation Environment: H200, `flashinfer 0.6.18`, `Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-seq-cls` (anchor `<|object_ref_start|>`), engine `float16` on `flashinfer`. ```bash # CPU unit tests (no GPU / model needed) python test/registered/unit/layers/test_pooler_score_and_pool.py -v python test/registered/unit/managers/test_setwise_score_mixin.py -v # E2E (GPU); setwise uses a SequenceClassification checkpoint export TEST_CLASSIFICATION_BASE_MODEL=/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-seq-cls python test/registered/e2e/scoring/test_setwise_scoring.py -v # Regression on the existing scoring paths export TEST_MODEL_NAME=/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct python test/registered/prefill_only/test_score_engine.py -v python test/registered/prefill_only/test_score_api.py -v python test/registered/prefill_only/test_serving_rerank.py -v ``` Results — all passing (106 cases): | Suite | Cases | Result | |---|---|---| | `test_pooler_score_and_pool.py` (CPU) | 12 | PASS | | `test_setwise_score_mixin.py` (CPU) | 44 | PASS | | `test_setwise_scoring.py` (E2E: HF-parity + MIS + mixed-batch + tokenized) | 10 | PASS | | `test_score_engine.py` (E2E regression) | 19 | PASS | | `test_score_api.py` (HTTP regression) | 8 | PASS | | `test_serving_rerank.py` (mock) | 13 | PASS | The E2E setwise tests assert **numerical parity** against a HuggingFace reference (gather the final hidden state at the anchor positions, apply the model's own classification head) — a wrong pooling position or head application changes the numbers, not just the shape. The MIS tests assert the nested per-item shape and block-diagonal set isolation (a set's scores are unchanged by other sets). ## Backward compatibility Purely additive. `score_extraction_token` / `score_extraction_token_id` default to `None`; when unset, the pointwise last-token path and its `[num_rows x num_labels]` shape are unchanged, as confirmed by the score-engine, score-api, and rerank regression suites. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #36041483134](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36041483134) Latest PR Test (Extra): :no_entry_sign: [Run #36041482839](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36041482839) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #36041483225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36041483225)

title: Fix MUSA detection under torch.compile fullgraph
body:
## Motivation

`is_musa()` performs a lazy optional import of `torchada`. When called from a
`torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` region on a system without `torchada`, Dynamo
unwraps the `lru_cache` wrapper and attempts to trace the import. This causes an
`Unsupported: Import failure` instead of returning `False`.

## Modifications

- Move lazy MUSA detection into a private cached helper.
- Mark the public `is_musa()` function with
`torch.compiler.assume_constant_result`.
- Preserve process-lifetime caching without triggering Dynamo's `lru_cache`
warning.
- Add a CPU-only regression test covering fullgraph compilation when `torchada`
is unavailable.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change does not affect model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. MUSA detection remains lazily evaluated and cached.

## Tests
```bash
  python test/registered/unit/utils/test_musa.py -v
  python3 scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash Day 0] Honor fused and per-expert names in quark `exclude`
body:
## Summary

Replacement for #37673, which GitHub closed when its deleted support base was merged into main. The original author and review history remain credited there.

`amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` contains BF16 layers that are explicitly excluded from MXFP4 quantization. Without this change, weight loading can allocate an MXFP4-packed parameter for one of those BF16 tensors and abort in `load_qkv_weight` with a 2x width mismatch:

```text
AssertionError: param_data.shape=torch.Size([128, 512]),
                loaded_weight.shape=torch.Size([128, 1024])
```

`should_ignore_layer()` currently checks `exclude` only after rewriting a fused module name into its component shards. GLM-5.3-Flash uses two exclusion forms that do not survive that rewrite:

1. **Already-fused modules named directly.** The vision tower serializes `visual.blocks.N.attn.qkv_proj` as one tensor and excludes that fused name directly. Expanding it to `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` misses the exclusion.
2. **Per-expert MoE exclusions.** The checkpoint lists `model.layers.{3,5,6}.mlp.experts.{0..287}.{down,gate,up}_proj`, while SGLang constructs one fused `model.layers.N.mlp.experts` module.

Measured on the original checkpoint used for #37673:

```text
exclude entries total                     2552
  ... mentioning "experts"                1860
  ... per-expert (experts.<N>.<proj>)     1728   -> layers 3, 5 and 6 only
  ... mentioning "visual"                  125
```

The affected expert tensors confirm the packed-versus-unpacked boundary:

```text
layers.5.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight   BF16   (4096, 2048)     no weight_scale
layers.7.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight   U8     (4096, 1024)     + weight_scale
```

At TP8, 2048/8 = **256** while 1024/8 = **128**, matching the original assertion exactly.

## Scope

Two files only:

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/utils.py`: honor a direct fused-module exclusion before packed-module expansion, and treat a fused `...experts` module as excluded when its individual experts are excluded.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_utils.py`: add non-vacuous bug catchers for both exclusion forms and regression guards for empty excludes, shard-level excludes, and unrelated expert layers.

The existing packed-shard path is unchanged when no direct match exists. The per-expert rule applies to whole-layer expert exclusions; SGLang cannot represent a checkpoint that mixes quantization schemes among experts inside one fused MoE module. No kernel, model forward path, backend policy, scheduler behavior, environment variable, or checkpoint tensor is changed.

## Test plan

Combined main-based integration (`RM/glm53-day0-main-integration` @ `22f233a853`, fresh checkpoint-specific caches):

- TP4 `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4@b5688f2549` on MI355X/gfx950: **20/20 GSM8K (100.00%)**, 100.00% stop rate, 0.00% truncation, 0.00% errors.
- The server loaded all 62 shards, completed decode graph capture, and returned a correct stopped generation (`17 + 25 = 42`).

Recovery base: `main` @ `6220f45d8e`.  
Replacement head: `25b9f7f658`.  
Original head: `de98483df0`.  
Container: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm724-mi35x-20260910` (`sha256:391afe1da11d`).  
Recovery validation on MI355X: scoped pre-commit passed; **15 unit tests passed**.

Original #37673 A/B validation used the same test cases in both arms:

| Arm | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | Directly excluded fused QKV and per-expert-to-fused-MoE cases fail; all three regression guards pass. |
| This PR | Both bug catchers and all three guards pass. |

| Check | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Registration | Existing CPU unit-test location; no GPU kernel is introduced |
| Formatting | Scoped pre-commit passed, including Ruff, format, codespell, and registered-test validation |
| Unit tests | `test_quark_utils.py`: **15 passed** |
| Accuracy | TP4 MXFP4 integration smoke: **100.00% GSM8K (20 examples)** |
| Speed | Not measured; this restores checkpoint loading semantics and does not modify execution kernels |

None of the other recovered Day-0 PRs modifies `quark/utils.py`; this exclusion gap is independent of their DSA, k-pool, mHC, MoE-runner, and TileLang changes.
